name: Chat with project context
description:
**Summary**

1. Started from a `ChatContext`/`ChatWithContext` wrapper carrying a "sprint board" into `chat_with_project`; both proposals were abandoned as too much plumbing.
2. Settled on reusing `Chat.mode == "agent"` as the orchestrator identity, with the completion signal already free in `Chat.status_history` and pause modelled as a `task_item == "pause_loop"` message marker (no schema change).
3. Answered the open questions: many agents per board, notify the **nearest** agent ancestor, completion = `status == "done"`, one run per completion, agent delegates (never implements), budget already exists, single report document, parallel runs.
4. First implementation was rejected — it rewrote `globals.py` and dropped 8 symbols (`ANALYTICS_DATA_PATH`, `LOGS_FOLDER`, `CODX_JUNIOR_HIDDEN`, …) — and it shipped a polling loop the user did not want.
5. Final change set: additive-only `globals.py` (4 constants), new `agent_notifier.py` (parent-agent walk, pause/budget/watermark gates, single-report collapse, **fire-and-forget** dispatch), and one hook in `ChatManager.save_chat`; `background.py` untouched.

messages.content:
We must create a chat context to pass when chatting with the project. 
This context will have important settings like the "sprint board" that will be use by project manager tools.
 
 It can be a wrapper model that has context and chat and pass it to the chat with project. context will be optional and pass to ai and tools.

Analyze

I'll analyze the current implementation to understand where a chat context wrapper can be introduced end-to-end.# Analysis — Chat context wrapper for `chat_with_project`

No files were modified. This is the design/impact analysis only.

---

## 1. Objective (restated)

- Introduce a **request-scoped context** that travels with a chat turn.
- The context carries **turn settings**, the first one being the **“sprint board”** (board / column / sprint / valid states) used by the **project manager tools**.
- Shape: a **wrapper model** = `context` + `chat`, passed into `chat_with_project`.
- `context` is **optional** (`None` ⇒ today’s behaviour, zero regressions).
- The context must reach **the AI** (prompt/model) **and the tools** (project manager).

---

## 2. Verified current flow (facts from the code)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant API as api/chat.py :: api_chat
    participant S as engine/session.py
    participant A as engine/chat_engine_actions.py
    participant E as chat/chat_engine.py
    participant AI as ai/ai.py
    participant SM as ai/smol/smol_agent.py
    participant T as tools/project_manager_tools.py

    C->>API: POST /api/chats {Chat json}
    API->>API: chat = Chat(**data)      %% unknown keys DROPPED
    API->>S: chat_with_project(chat)
    S->>A: chat_with_project(chat, system=GLOBAL_CHAT_INSTRUCTIONS)
    A->>E: ChatEngine(...).chat_with_project(chat, system=...)
    E->>E: resolve profiles/tools, build messages
    E->>AI: a_chat_run(messages, tools, run_context, current_chat, vision_content)
    AI->>SM: chat(messages, config)
    SM->>SM: settings._active_session = session; session._current_chat = chat
    SM->>T: tool_call(**params + settings + tool_cache)
```

Touch points that already exist (and would need to carry the new context):

| # | File | Relevant fact |
|---|------|---------------|
| 1 | `codx/junior/api/chat.py` | `api_chat` builds `chat = Chat(**data)` and calls `session.chat_with_project(chat=chat)`. Extra JSON keys are **silently ignored** by pydantic. |
| 2 | `codx/junior/sio/sio.py` + `sio/model.py` | `io_chat` → `SioChatMessage(**data)` → same call. |
| 3 | `codx/junior/engine/session.py` | `chat_with_project(...)` delegates to `_chat_engine_actions`. |
| 4 | `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py` | Creates a fresh `ChatEngine`; injects `system=GLOBAL_CHAT_INSTRUCTIONS`; saves chat afterwards. |
| 5 | `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `chat_with_project` → `_chat_with_project_inner` (token registry, bridge, profiles, `get_ai`, `_execute_ai_response`, agent recursion, `switch_project` delegation). |
| 6 | `codx/junior/ai/ai.py` | `AI.__init__(settings, llm_model, user, system, session)`; `a_chat_run` builds the `config` dict forwarded to SmolAgent. |
| 7 | `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | `_execute_tool` injects `settings` (if `ToolSettings.project_settings`) and `tool_cache` (**only if the signature declares it**). |
| 8 | `codx/junior/tools/model.py` | `ToolSettings` already declares `session: bool` — but SmolAgent **never injects `session`**. |
| 9 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | Resolves `settings`/`session`/`current_chat` from `kwargs` + `settings._active_session`; validates board/column/sprint/state against `tasks/kanban.json` (`_validate_task_location`). |
| 10 | `codx/junior/db.py` | `Chat` already has `board`, `column`, `sprints`, `status`, `priority`, `due_date`, `assignees`. |
| 11 | `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` | Owns `STATUS_ORDER` / `PRIORITY_ORDER` — the canonical catalogue the tool validates against. |
| 12 | `engine/agent_runtime.py` | `AgentRunContext` — **different concept** (event fan-out, cancellation, analytics). |

---

## 3. Why a wrapper model is required (constraints found)

1. **`Chat(**data)` swallows unknown keys.** Adding `"context"` next to the chat fields in the request body would be silently discarded → invisible bug. Either the body must be restructured (`{ "chat": {...}, "context": {...} }`) or the endpoint must read `context` explicitly *before* constructing `Chat`.
2. **Context must not be persisted on `Chat`.** `ChatManager.save_chat` serialises the whole model to `.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/*.json`. A transient sprint selection would become stale state, duplicate itself into every sub-task created by `generate_tasks`, and change `Chat` schema/serialisation for all clients.
3. **The only existing “context” channels are implicit and mutable**:
   - `self.settings._active_session = self.session`
   - `self.session._current_chat = current_chat`

   Both are attributes stamped on shared objects — the wrong pattern for a per-request value that can differ between concurrent runs on the same project settings instance.
4. **Tools cannot be given a mandatory parameter.** `_execute_tool` calls `tool["tool_call"](**params)`; injecting `chat_context` unconditionally would raise `TypeError` for every tool whose signature has no `**kwargs`.
5. **Naming collisions to avoid**: `AgentRunContext` (runtime/events) and the `team_context` tool already exist.

---

## 4. Proposed model

New module `codx/junior/model/chat_context.py` (pure pydantic, no imports from `engine`/`chat` to avoid cycles — `codx.junior.model.planning` is the closest precedent):

```py
class SprintBoardContext(BaseModel):
    board: Optional[str] = None          # default destination board
    column: Optional[str] = None         # default destination column
    sprint: Optional[str] = None         # sprint id (a "sprint" board)
    sprints: List[str] = []              # optional: several sprints in scope
    states: List[str] = []               # catalogue snapshot (optional)
    board_columns: List[str] = []        # catalogue snapshot (optional)
    default_status: Optional[str] = None # initial state for created tasks

class ChatContext(BaseModel):
    sprint_board: Optional[SprintBoardContext] = None
    project_ids: List[str] = []
    user: Optional[CodxUser] = None
    variables: Dict[str, Any] = {}       # extension point (no schema churn)
    # future: tool allow-list, model/mode overrides, guardrail scope

class ChatRequest(BaseModel):            # the wrapper requested in the task
    chat: Chat
    context: Optional[ChatContext] = None
```

Request example (backwards compatible parsing: if the body has no `chat` key, treat it as `Chat` plus optional `context`):

```json
{
  "chat": { "id": "...", "name": "Sprint 12 review", "messages": [ ... ] },
  "context": {
    "sprint_board": { "board": "Sprint 12", "column": "tasks", "sprint": "Sprint 12", "default_status": "todo" },
    "project_ids": ["<project-id>"]
  }
}
```

TypeScript-side mirror (for the client) is just the same shape; nothing is persisted.

### Resolution precedence (single rule, applied in the tool)

```
explicit tool argument  >  context.sprint_board  >  chat.board / chat.sprints / chat.column  >  defaults (kanban / tasks / todo)
```

This makes the context a **default provider**, not an override, so the model can still contradict it deliberately (and the existing catalogue validation still applies).

---

## 5. Propagation plan (files → change)

| File | Change | Why |
|------|--------|-----|
| `codx/junior/model/chat_context.py` **(new)** | `ChatContext`, `SprintBoardContext`, `ChatRequest`, `to_prompt_block()` | Single definition, no cycles |
| `codx/junior/api/chat.py` | `api_chat`: read `context` from body (wrapper or legacy shape), validate sprint board against the catalogue, forward `context=` to `session.chat_with_project` | Entry point (the working file of this task) |
| `codx/junior/sio/model.py`, `codx/junior/sio/sio.py` | `SioChatMessage.context: Optional[ChatContext]`; forward | Socket.IO parity |
| `codx/junior/engine/session.py` | `chat_with_project(..., context=None)` → delegate | Keep the public session signature consistent |
| `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py` | Forward `context` into `ChatEngine.chat_with_project`; optionally append the context block to `GLOBAL_CHAT_INSTRUCTIONS` | Session→engine bridge |
| `codx/junior/engine.py` (legacy duplicate `chat_with_project`) | Same parameter or explicitly documented as legacy/deprecated | Avoid a silent behaviour split |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `chat_with_project(..., context=None)` → `_chat_with_project_inner(..., context=...)` → `get_ai(..., context=...)` → `_execute_ai_response(..., context=...)`; **also forward** in the `switch_project` delegation and in the agent-iteration recursion | 4 mandatory forwarding points |
| `codx/junior/ai/ai.py` | `AI.__init__(chat_context=None)`; `a_chat_run(..., chat_context=None)` → `config["chat_context"]` | Reaches SmolAgent |
| `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | Store `chat_context`; in `_execute_tool` inject `params["chat_context"]` **only if** `inspect.signature(...)` declares it (mirroring `tool_cache`); inject **after** computing the cache key or exclude it from the key | Tool delivery without breaking signatures/caching |
| `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | Accept `context`/`chat_context`; use `context.sprint_board` as default board/column/sprint/status; scope `list_tasks`/`list_boards` to the active sprint | The consumer this feature exists for |

Tool opt-in sketch (recommended pattern, consistent with `tool_cache`):

```py
async def project_manager(action: str, ..., context: Optional[ChatContext] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    ...
    defaults = _defaults_from_context(context, chat=_current_chat(**kwargs))
    board  = board  or defaults.board
    column = column or defaults.column
    sprint = sprint or defaults.sprint
```

---

## 6. Behaviour matrix

| Situation | Expected behaviour |
|---|---|
| `context is None` | Exactly today’s behaviour; tool falls back to `chat.board` / `chat.sprints` / defaults |
| `context.sprint_board.board` unknown | Fail fast at the API boundary (`422`) **or** log-warn + ignore (see open question) |
| Context present, model passes explicit `board` | Explicit argument wins; catalogue validation unchanged |
| Agent recursion (`is_agent`, `iterations > 0`) | Context must be re-forwarded, otherwise it disappears after iteration 1 |
| `switch_project(turn_project_id)` delegation | Context must be forwarded; `sprint_board` belongs to the *target* project’s catalogue |
| `project_manager(action="request_changes")` nested run | Decision needed: inherit context only when the task’s `sprints` include the active sprint, else drop |
| Auxiliary AI calls (`_generate_chat_description`, `_auto_initialize_chat_metadata`, summaries) | Pass `context=None` — no sprint semantics |

---

## 7. Risks & edge cases

1. **Tool cache key.** `ToolCache.get_cache_key` does `json.dumps(params)`. Injected non-JSON values make hashing fail → `cache_key = ""` → the result is silently **not cached**. Note that today `params["settings"]` is already injected *before* `tool_cache.set(...)`, so `project_settings` tools are effectively uncached. Adding `chat_context` must not make this worse: inject it after `get()` and strip it before `set()` (or hash a stable projection of it).
2. **`settings._active_session` remains a shared-mutable hazard.** Two concurrent turns on the same project settings object can see each other’s session/chat. Do not extend that mechanism for the context — thread it explicitly.
3. **Persistence leakage.** Any field added to `Chat` ends up in `.codx/tasks/**/*.json`, in `Chat.model_dump()` payloads to the client, and in sub-task copies created by `generate_tasks` / `process_task`. Keep `ChatContext` ephemeral.
4. **Signature-driven injection is the only safe option** (`**params` call site). A `ToolSettings.context: bool` flag can be added for symmetry, but signature inspection is what actually prevents `TypeError`.
5. **Guardrail / prompt growth.** If the context is injected into the system prompt, keep it to a small deterministic block (`<chat_context>` with board/column/sprint/states) and only when `context` is present.
6. **Catalogue staleness.** A client-supplied `board_columns`/`states` snapshot must never override `kanban.json` validation in `_validate_task_location`; the snapshot is informational only.
7. **Sub-task inheritance.** `generate_tasks` and the project-manager tool spawn *new* chats; decide explicitly whether the sprint context is inherited (recommended: no, unless the created chat declares the same `sprints`).

---

## 8. Open questions (blocking a precise implementation)

1. **Transport shape**: accept the wrapper `{ "chat": ..., "context": ... }` (clean, explicit) and keep the legacy flat body as a fallback — or context only via header/query?
2. **Invalid sprint board**: `422` at the API (fail fast) or “warn + ignore” (never break a chat)?
3. **Persistence**: is the sprint board purely per-turn, or must it be remembered per chat across turns (in which case `Chat.sprints`/`board` are the storage, and the context only *seeds* them)?
4. **Scope of the context**: only `sprint_board` for now, or also `project_ids` / tool allow-list / model override?
5. **Nested runs**: should `request_changes`, sub-task generation and `mention_manager` inherit the context?
6. **Smartphone/desktop client**: which UI currently sends `Chat` — is a wrapper payload acceptable, or must the backend keep the flat body 100% unchanged?

---

## 9. Suggested implementation order (once the questions above are answered)

1. `model/chat_context.py` (models only, no wiring).
2. `api/chat.py` + `sio` (parse & validate, forward).
3. `engine/session.py` → `chat_engine_actions.py` → `chat_engine.py` (threading + recursion + `switch_project`).
4. `ai/ai.py` → `smol_agent.py` (config + opt-in injection).
5. `tools/project_manager_tools.py` (defaults + scope), then the other task tools.
6. Optional: `<chat_context>` block in the system prompt.

```py codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py
"""
Project manager tools for codx-junior.

These tools let a profile (AI role) act as a **project manager** over the
project's kanban tasks (each task is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in
``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/``). They cover the day-to-day workflow:

    - ``create_task``     : create a new task chat associated to a kanban
                            board + column and one or more sprints.
    - ``get_task``        : review a task (status, board/column, sprints and
                            the visible conversation).
    - ``list_tasks``      : list/filter tasks (board, column, sprint, status,
                            free-text).
    - ``list_boards``     : discover the kanban boards, their columns, the
                            sprint boards and the valid task states (so names
                            are known before creating or moving a task).
    - ``update_task``     : change the task status and/or move it between
                            boards, columns and sprints (and edit priority,
                            due date, progress, assignees and tags).
    - ``request_changes`` : add a comment **and** process the task through
                            :class:`~codx.junior.chat.chat_engine.ChatEngine`
                            (``session.chat_with_project``).
    - ``request_help``    : add a comment **without** triggering the engine
                            (ask the user for help / leave a note).

Design notes:
    - **One tool, several actions.** Keeping the workflow unified (like
      ``team_management``/``profile_management``) avoids spending prompt tokens
      on a schema per action and keeps the mental model small.
    - **Nothing duplicated.** Tasks are plain chats: this module never
      re-implements persistence, it delegates to
      :class:`~codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager`
      (``save_chat`` / ``update_chat_metadata`` / ``find_by_id`` / ``list_chats``).
      ``update_chat_metadata`` keeps messages intact and records a
      ``ChatStatusEvent`` on every real status transition, so task-performance
      metrics keep working.
    - **Processing is explicit.** Only ``request_changes`` runs the engine;
      ``request_help`` only writes a comment. A background run preserves the
      coroutine reference so it is not garbage-collected.
    - **Strict destination validation.** A task can NEVER be stored on a board,
      a column, a sprint or a state that does not exist: those values are
      validated against the project catalogue (``tasks/kanban.json`` and the
      states owned by :mod:`codx.junior.planning_manager`) and an invalid value
      is rejected with an error that lists the available options and asks to
      create the missing one first. The catalogue spelling is also enforced, so
      ``bugs`` resolves to the existing ``Bugs`` board instead of creating a
      phantom ``.codx/tasks/bugs`` folder.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.db import Chat, Message

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Actions exposed by the tool (canonical names).
VALID_ACTIONS = [
    "list_boards",
    "list_tasks",
    "get_task",
    "create_task",
    "update_task",
    "request_changes",
    "request_help",
]

# Tolerant aliases so a slightly different verb never crashes the run.
ACTION_ALIASES = {
    "boards": "list_boards",

    "get": "get_task",
    "read": "get_task",

"""
Unified logging, event emission and cancellation for agent runs.
Wraps openai_ai without modifying it: openai_ai's stream/tool callbacks
are adapted onto AgentRunContext.
"""
import json
import logging
import threading

class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token. cancel() may be called from any thread
    (e.g. a Socket.IO 'stop' handler) while the agent loop runs elsewhere."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._event = threading.Event()
        self.reason: str | None = None

    def cancel(self, reason: str = "user_requested"):
        self.reason = reason
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    def raise_if_cancelled(self):
        if self._event.is_set():
            raise AgentCancelled(self.reason or "cancelled")

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent):

            stats = self.tool_calls.setdefault(

            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:

    def summary(self) -> dict:

                "completion_tokens": self.completion_tokens,

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,

    Function will return the final code.

    Args:
        code_text (str): The code to which best practices should be applied.

        file_list=[file_path],
        messages=[HumanMessage(content=message_content)]
    )

Tool execution cache manager for SmolAgent.

Caches tool results based on tool name and arguments hash to avoid

import hashlib

CacheEntry = Tuple[Any, bool]  # (result, was_successful)


class ToolCache:
    """

    Cached results:
    - Bypass tool loop guards (don't count towards max_tool_calls)
    - Emit TOOL_START/END events with `cached=True` for observability
    - Are immediately sent to the model without re-execution
    """

        """Initialize an empty tool cache."""
        self._cache: Dict[str, CacheEntry] = {}
        self._hit_count: int = 0
        self._miss_count: int = 0

        self, tool_name: str, params: Dict[str, Any]

        Uses SHA256 hash of (tool_name, sorted JSON params) to ensure
        identical calls always produce the same key, regardless of dict

            params:    Arguments dictionary passed to the tool.

                cache_key_input.encode("utf-8")
            ).hexdigest()

            # If params can't be serialized, return None to skip caching
            logger.debug(

Notes:
 - "context.sprint_board" will be the board's name, not and object.Tools can use sprint name to find the sprint object.
 -  Context won't be in the chat, instead a new ChatWithContext (or so) model will have both elements (optional context)
 
Review

I'll ground the review in the actual code before adjusting the design.# Review — Chat context (`ChatWithContext` + `context.sprint_board` as a name)

No files modified. Review of the previous design with the two corrections applied, verified against the current code.

---

## 1. Corrections applied

| # | Previous design | Now | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `context.sprint_board: SprintBoardContext` (board/column/sprint/states snapshot object) | `context.sprint_board: Optional[str]` — **the sprint/board name**; tools resolve it against `tasks/kanban.json` | No parallel sprint model, no snapshot to go stale, no duplicated catalogue. `ChatContext` becomes trivially JSON-serializable |
| 2 | Context was going to be added to `Chat` (and parsed out of the request body) | Context **never** touches `Chat`; a new wrapper `ChatWithContext{chat, context?}` is the request model | No `db.py` change, no `ChatManager` change, no persistence leak into `.codx/tasks/**/*.json`, no change to `Chat.model_dump()` payloads sent to clients |

Both changes remove risk rather than add it. The remaining design is *smaller* than the previous one.

---

## 2. Why the string is the right call (evidence from the code)

The sprint dimension is **already identified by board name** everywhere:

* `db.py` → `Chat.sprints: List[str]` — *"Identifiers of the sprint boards this chat belongs to"*.
* `tools/project_manager_tools.py::_validate_task_location` → every sprint is validated with
  `_match_board(by_name=_board_catalogue(kanban), board=sprint)` — i.e. **a sprint is looked up in the board catalogue**.
* `_action_list_tasks` → `chats = [c for c in chats if sprint in (c.sprints or [])]`.
* `_boards_info` already computes `is_sprint` per board (`type == "sprint"`).

So `sprint_board: str` is *the native type of the whole sprint axis*. Consequences:

```py
# tool side — one lookup, catalogue stays the single source of truth
board_info = _match_board(by_name=_board_catalogue(kanban), board=context.sprint_board)
sprint = board_info["name"] if board_info else None        # canonical spelling
```

* Validation stays where it already is (`kanban.json` + `planning_manager.STATUS_ORDER`) — the context can never become a second source of truth.
* Renaming a sprint board in the UI requires **zero** context-model changes.
* The context payload is `{"sprint_board": "Sprint 12"}` — a few bytes on every turn.

**New risk the string introduces (needs handling):** `_action_list_tasks` filters with raw string equality, *without* case/alias normalisation. `create_task`/`update_task` canonicalise through `_validate_task_location`, but `list_tasks` does not. Therefore any context-derived sprint used as a **filter** must be canonicalised first through `_match_board` (case-insensitive) — otherwise `"sprint 12"` silently returns zero tasks.

---

## 3. Revised model

New module `codx/junior/model/chat_context.py` (pydantic only + `Chat`, same import shape already used by `sio/model.py`):

```py
class ChatContext(BaseModel):
    """Ephemeral, request-scoped settings for one chat turn. Never persisted."""
    sprint_board: Optional[str] = None      # sprint board NAME (a sprint is a board)
    project_ids: List[str] = []             # optional extra project scope
    variables: Dict[str, Any] = {}          # extension point, no schema churn

class ChatWithContext(BaseModel):
    """Request wrapper: the chat plus optional per-turn context."""
    chat: Chat
    context: Optional[ChatContext] = None
```

Notes to review:

* **`ChatContext` is frozen at turn level.** It is not stored anywhere, therefore it must be **re-sent by the client on every turn** — including the tool-driven `request_changes` re-entries if sprint scope should survive them. This is a deliberate trade for zero persistence risk (see §8).
* **Naming.** Use `chat_context` (not `context`) in code signatures: `AgentRunContext` (event runtime), `ToolContext` (`ai/smol/tool_context.py`) and the `team_context` tool already exist. `ChatContext` is unambiguous only if we stop calling it bare `context` inside the engine.
* `sprint_board` is **one** name by design. `Chat.sprints` is a list, but the context expresses *"the sprint I am working in"*, which is singular. Anything wider is a `project_ids`/`variables` concern.

---

## 4. Transport: wrapper vs legacy body

`api/chat.py::api_chat` currently does `chat = Chat(**data)`; pydantic v1 **ignores** unknown keys, so an inline `"context"` next to the chat fields would be silently dropped (invisible bug). With the wrapper the body becomes:

```json
{ "chat": { "id": "...", "messages": [ ... ] },
  "context": { "sprint_board": "Sprint 12" } }
```

Parsing rule to make both shapes work:

```py
payload = await request.json()
if isinstance(payload.get("chat"), dict):
    request_model = ChatWithContext(**payload)          # new shape
    chat, chat_context = request_model.chat, request_model.context
else:
    chat_context_data = payload.pop("context", None)     # legacy flat shape
    chat = Chat(**payload)
    chat_context = ChatContext(**chat_context_data) if chat_context_data else None
```

Review points on this entry point:

* Response shape is unchanged (returns `chat`) → no client breakage on the read path.
* **Bug to fix in the same edit:** the `except` branch of `api_chat` currently returns `"chat_id": data.get("id")`, which is `None` for the wrapper shape. It must use the resolved `chat.id`.
* `ChatWithContext` should be permissive (`context: Optional[...] = None`) so an unchanged client keeps working forever.
* Same treatment for Socket.IO: `sio/model.py::SioChatMessage` gets `context: Optional[ChatContext] = None`, `sio.py::io_chat` forwards it. `codx-junior-generate-tasks` / improve handlers stay untouched.

---

## 5. Propagation map (revised)

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `codx/junior/model/chat_context.py` **(new)** | `ChatContext`, `ChatWithContext`, `to_prompt_block()` | One definition, no engine imports |
| `codx/junior/api/chat.py` | Parse wrapper/legacy, forward `context=`; fix `chat_id` in the error branch | Entry point |
| `codx/junior/sio/model.py` + `sio/sio.py` | `SioChatMessage.context`, forward in `io_chat` | Socket.IO parity |
| `codx/junior/engine/session.py` | `chat_with_project(..., context=None)` → delegate | Public session signature |
| `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py` | Forward `context` into `ChatEngine.chat_with_project` | Session→engine bridge |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `chat_with_project(..., context=None)` → `_chat_with_project_inner(..., context=...)` → `get_ai(..., context=...)` → `_execute_ai_response(..., context=...)`; **forward in the `switch_project` delegation and in the agent recursion (step 24)**; append the prompt block next to `final_system_prompt` | 4 mandatory forwarding points |
| `codx/junior/ai/ai.py` | `a_chat_run(..., chat_context=None)` → `config["chat_context"]` | Reaches SmolAgent |
| `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | Read `config["chat_context"]` per run; pass to `_execute_tool`; inject **only if the tool declares it** | Tool delivery |

Forgetting either `switch_project` (line: `return await engine.chat_with_project(chat=chat, ...)`) or the recursion at step 24 makes the context **vanish after the first hop / iteration** — this is the most likely real bug of the whole feature.

---

## 6. Tool contract

**Injection.** Follow the `tool_cache` pattern (signature-driven), not the `project_settings` flag:

```py
# smol_agent._execute_tool
if chat_context is not None:
    try:
        sig = inspect.signature(tool["tool_call"])
        if "chat_context" in sig.parameters:
            params["chat_context"] = chat_context
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        pass
```

Two specific cautions:

1. **Do not** fall back to "tool has `**kwargs`" for detection. `project_manager` ends with `**kwargs`, so a VAR_KEYWORD fallback would inject into *every* `**kwargs` tool. Instead declare it explicitly:
   `async def project_manager(action: str, ..., chat_context: Optional[ChatContext] = None, **kwargs)` — then declared-name detection is exact and the TOOLS registry needs no change.
2. **Inject `chat_context.model_dump()`, not the model instance.** `ToolCache.get_cache_key` does `json.dumps(params, sort_keys=True)`; a pydantic model raises → `cache_key = ""` → the call is silently not cached. A plain dict hashes fine.

**Pre-existing cache-key mismatch worth fixing now (small, adjacent):** in `_execute_tool`, `params["settings"] = self.settings` happens **before** `tool_cache.set(func_name, params, ...)`, while `tool_cache.get(...)` in the loop used pristine args → keys never match, so `project_settings` tools are effectively uncached today. Adding `chat_context` repeats that. Fix: snapshot the pristine args at the top of `_execute_tool` and use them for `set()`.

**Consumer defaults (precedence, one rule):**

```
explicit tool argument > context.sprint_board > chat.sprints / chat.board > DEFAULT_*
```

* `create_task`: `sprints = sprints or ([sprint] if sprint else None) or ([ctx.sprint_board] if ctx.sprint_board else None)`.
* `list_tasks`: `sprint = sprint or canonical(ctx.sprint_board)` — **canonicalise before filtering** (§2).
* `list_boards`: optionally mark the active sprint in the output (informational only).
* `update_task`: do **not** default from context — silently moving tasks into the sprint on any update is a surprising side effect.
* `request_changes` / `request_help`: nothing to default.

**Validation policy (recommended split):**

| Origin of the value | Policy |
|---|---|
| Model-provided argument | Strict — unchanged `_validate_task_location` error listing available options |
| Context-provided default | Lenient — resolve via `_match_board`; if unknown or `not is_sprint`, **drop it, log a warning and say so in the tool response** |

Rationale: a stale sprint name in a client payload must never make `create_task` fail. The strict contract only applies to what the model explicitly asked for.

---

## 7. What we deliberately do **not** do

* No field on `Chat` / `Message` → `.codx/tasks/**/*.json`, `Chat.model_dump()` responses and `generate_tasks` sub-task copies remain byte-identical.
* No `ChatManager` / `planning_manager` change.
* No `board_columns` / `states` snapshot in the context — `kanban.json` stays the only catalogue.
* No extension of `settings._active_session` / `session._current_chat`. Those are shared mutable stamps on a per-project object; two concurrent turns can see each other's state. The context is threaded **explicitly** as a parameter instead.
* No context on auxiliary AI calls: `_generate_chat_description` and `_auto_initialize_chat_metadata` reuse the `ai_chat` closure — they must call it **without** `chat_context`/`run_context` (same pattern already used for `run_context`).

---

## 8. Behaviour matrix

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Client sends legacy flat body | `context = None` → byte-for-byte today's behaviour |
| `context` present, `sprint_board` = valid sprint | `create_task`/`list_tasks` default to it; prompt block added |
| `context.sprint_board` unknown / not a sprint board | warn + ignore (never fails the chat); tool response notes it |
| Model passes an explicit `sprint`/`board` | Explicit wins; strict validation unchanged |
| Agent recursion (iteration ≥ 1) | Must be re-forwarded, else context disappears after iteration 1 |
| `switch_project` (turn project differs) | Must be forwarded; the sprint name belongs to the **target** project catalogue |
| `generate_tasks` / `process_task` sub-tasks | Not inherited (sub-task chats are created from `chat.board`/`chat.column`); decide explicitly |
| Aux summaries / auto-init | No context |

---

## 9. Remaining risks

1. **Missing forwarding points** (recursion, `switch_project`, and the legacy `codx/junior/engine.py`) — the highest-probability defect; add a log line `chat_context sprint_board=... (turn %d)` on each hop to make regressions visible.
2. **Silent no-op on `list_tasks`** due to raw string matching vs canonical catalogue spelling (§2).
3. **Cache-key mismatch** — pre-existing; do not make it worse (`model_dump()` + pristine-args `set()`).
4. **Prompt growth** — keep the block to 1–3 lines, only when `context` is present, and place it *before* `CONVERSATION_GUARDRAIL_SYSTEM_PROMPT` so the guardrail stays last.
5. **Client discipline** — no persistence means the client must resend the sprint on every turn; if it forgets, the turn silently behaves as today (acceptable, but document it).
6. **Case sensitivity in `Chat.sprints`** — stored values are canonicalised on write, so filtering must use canonical names too.

---

## 10. Open questions (reduced to 4)

1. **Unknown `sprint_board`**: warn+ignore (recommended) or `422` at `POST /chats`?
2. **Prompt block**: yes (recommended, tiny) or tools-only injection?
3. **Sub-task inheritance**: should `generate_tasks` / `process_task` propagate `sprint_board` (recommended: no, unless the child chat declares the same sprint)?
4. **Scope now**: only `sprint_board` (recommended for the first iteration) or also `project_ids` / tool allow-list?

---

## 11. Suggested implementation order

1. `model/chat_context.py` — models only, no wiring.
2. `api/chat.py` + `sio/model.py` + `sio/sio.py` — parse both shapes, forward, fix `chat_id` in the error branch.
3. `engine/session.py` → `engine/chat_engine_actions.py` → `chat/chat_engine.py` — threading, recursion, `switch_project`, prompt block.
4. `ai/ai.py` → `ai/smol/smol_agent.py` — `config["chat_context"]` + signature-driven injection (plain dict).
5. `tools/project_manager_tools.py` — `chat_context` param, canonical sprint default for `create_task`/`list_tasks`, lenient validation.
6. Optional: pristine-args fix for `ToolCache.set`, active-sprint highlight in `list_boards`.

# The "orchestrator" chat mode
What if instead the chat context we use something we already have: chat mode

## orchestrator mode
One task in the board acts as a ProjectManager, with instructions and profiles defined by user.
The orchestrator is the main interaction point of the user, acts as a single document with a report and every time is invoked does the job and generates a report.

Main difference is that when other tasks in the same board/sprint as the orchestrator finish, an event will be rise to process the orchrestrator task again. In other to stop the loop, use can (chat mode ...bit dirty, add a comment, "pause the loop", or add new setting in chat to pause the loop)

----
review and create pros & cons

I'll ground this review in the code — chat-mode plumbing, task-completion signals, and the event store that would drive the loop.Search results mix duplicated snapshots. Reading the authoritative files directly.Verifying cost/status-event fields before asserting them in the review.# Review — “orchestrator” chat mode instead of a chat context

No files modified. This is a design review with pros & cons, grounded in the current code.

---

## 1. Objective (restated)

- Reuse **`Chat.mode`** (already persisted, already round-tripped) instead of introducing a `ChatContext` / `ChatWithContext` wrapper.
- New mode `orchestrator`: one task on a board **is** the project manager.
  - Instructions + profiles defined by the user (both mechanisms already exist).
  - The user’s main interaction point; behaves like a **single document** with a report.
  - Every invocation re-does the job and regenerates the report.
- **Trigger:** when other tasks in the same board/sprint finish, an event re-invokes the orchestrator.
- **Stop condition:** the user must be able to pause the loop. Three candidate mechanisms (mode change / “pause the loop” comment / new Chat setting) are flagged as “dirty”.

---

## 2. Verdict up front

**Adopt the mode as the identity. Do not encode the loop state in it.**

| Aspect | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `mode="orchestrator"` as the chat’s **identity/behaviour** | ✅ Strong — deletes most of the previous proposal’s surface |
| `mode` as the **loop lifecycle** (paused/running) | ❌ Not recommended — conflates behaviour with scheduling |
| Completion **event** source | ⚠️ Does not exist yet in a usable form — see §5.3, this is the real work |
| Re-invocation loop | ⚠️ Needs coalescing + per-chat lock + budget, none of which exist |

Two of the three “dirty” stop options are symptoms of the same missing piece: **identity (what this chat is)** and **run state (may it be re-invoked)** are orthogonal and deserve separate storage.

---

## 3. What this deletes from the previous design

| Previous (`ChatContext`) | Orchestrator mode | Net |
|---|---|---|
| New `model/chat_context.py` (`ChatContext`, `ChatWithContext`) | Not needed — `Chat.mode` exists | −1 module |
| `api/chat.py` parses wrapper vs legacy flat body; fixes `chat_id` in `error` branch | Unchanged: `chat = Chat(**data)` already carries `mode` | −1 parser, −1 compat rule |
| `sio/model.py::SioChatMessage.context`, `sio.py::io_chat` forwarding | Unchanged | −2 edits |
| Thread `context=` through `engine/session.py`, `chat_engine_actions.py`, `chat_engine.py` (4 forwarding points), `ai/ai.py`, `ai/smol/smol_agent.py` | **Zero** threading — `mode` is read inside `ChatEngine` where it already resolves flags | −6 files of plumbing |
| Tools receive `chat_context` via signature-driven injection into `_execute_tool` | Tools reach tasks through `settings._active_session` / `session` — already how `project_manager` works | −1 injection mechanism |

That is the single biggest **pro**: the transport, persistence and tool-delivery problems of the previous proposal simply disappear. `Chat.mode` is `str = "chat"` in `db.py`, is written to `.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/*.json` by `ChatManager.store_chat`, and arrives untouched through both `api_chat` and `SioChatMessage`. Even the previous review’s open questions #1 (transport shape) and #6 (client payload compat) become moot.

---

## 4. Pros

### P1 — Identity is persisted, discoverable and auditable
`mode` lives in the chat JSON. A background scanner can therefore answer *“which chats are orchestrators for sprint X?”* by reading files — exactly what a scheduler needs. The `ChatContext` design had no way to discover “who the PM is” without the client re-announcing it on every turn (a documented risk previously: forget to resend ⇒ silent no-op).

### P2 — “A task in the board acts as ProjectManager” is already literal
`planning_manager._is_task` only excludes `mode == "chat"` chats **without** planning signal. Any chat with another mode is a task → it appears in `query_tasks`, `build_dashboard`, metrics and `board_progress` with **zero query changes**. It already has `board`, `column`, `sprints`, `status`, `priority`, `assignees`, `sort_index`.

### P3 — “Instructions and profiles defined by user” needs no new model
`Chat.profiles` + `Profile` (`content`, `tools`, `llm_model`, `chat_mode`, `guardrails`, `profiles` for linked expansion) already delivers this. `_resolve_profiles_and_model` merges them into the system prompt and `chat_tools`; `project_manager` is reachable as soon as a profile lists it.

### P4 — One branch point for behaviour
`_resolve_chat_mode_flags` already returns a dict of booleans from the resolved mode and emits a single log line. Adding `is_orchestrator` follows the established pattern and keeps `_chat_with_project_inner` readable.

### P5 — “Single document with a report” has an existing implementation
`_hide_non_answer_messages(chat)` is already applied for `task`/`tutorial`/`vibe`: keep `is_answer` messages visible, hide the rest. An orchestrator report can reuse it verbatim — no new rendering concept.

### P6 — The event store already exists and already records completion
`PlanningEventStore` writes `<codx_path>/planning/events.jsonl`, one line per changed field, with `actor`, `action`, `from_value`/`to_value`, `timestamp`. `PlanningManager._emit_update_events` maps `status → "completed"` when the new status is in `DONE_STATUSES`. A per-sprint “what finished since my last report?” query is a filter over an append-only file — no new infrastructure.

### P7 — The polling host already exists
`background.py::check_projects` already fans out over all projects every `PROJECT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 3` in a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, with a per-thread `asyncio.run(...)` and a quarantine/backoff mechanism for failures. An orchestrator scan is the same shape and inherits restart resilience for free.

### P8 — Cost/actor bookkeeping is already wired
`ChatEngine` stamps `Message.cost` / `cost_info` per run and documents accumulation into `Chat.cost` compared against `Chat.estimation_cost`; `Analytics.record_chat_session` records mode/profiles/files/model per session (and `mode` is literally one of its fields). An unattended loop is at least **observable** the day it ships.

---

## 5. Cons

### C1 — `mode` conflates two orthogonal axes *(design, medium)*

Today `mode` answers *“how does the model behave during this turn?”* (`chat` / `task` / `tutorial` / `vibe` / `agent`). The orchestrator also needs *“may this chat be re-invoked, and when?”* — a lifecycle property.

Consequences:

- Flag explosion: is an orchestrator also refine? agent? Does it hide non-answers? Each future mode multiplies the matrix.
- **A mode edit silently changes lifecycle.** Switching the chat to `task` to refine a document, or to `agent` for one long run, stops the loop as a side effect — invisible, and exactly the kind of coupling that produces “why did it stop?” bug reports.
- **“Paused” is not expressible.** Pausing by changing mode destroys the identity, so resuming requires remembering the previous value somewhere else — you end up storing loop state anyway, just implicitly.

### C2 — The three stop-the-loop options, compared *(this is where “bit dirty” comes from)*

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Change `chat.mode` | no new field; UI already edits mode | destroys identity; can’t distinguish *paused* from *reconfigured*; resume needs hidden memory; any legitimate mode switch stops the loop |
| Comment “pause the loop” | zero schema; visible + auditable in the conversation; usable from chat or via `request_help` | prompt-level: the model may ignore it; needs parsing; **you pay for the invocation that reads it**; fragile to typos/translation; not machine-checkable by the scheduler before spending tokens |
| New `Chat` setting (e.g. `loop: {enabled, paused_reason, runs, last_run_at}`) | checked *before* any token spend; explicit in UI; serialized with the chat; room for run counters and watermarks | one more persisted field |

The third option is the only one the **scheduler** can honour cheaply. A persisted field is also low-risk here: `Chat(**data)` tolerates absent keys (pydantic defaults), and `auto_initialize` is existing precedent for a transient chat-level flag. Recommend `mode="orchestrator"` + a separate `loop` block, and let pause be `loop.enabled = false` — not a mode change, not a comment.

### C3 — There is no durable completion signal today *(correctness, high — the main risk)*

Verified paths for a status change:

| Writer | Persisted signal |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/planning/tasks/{id}` → `PlanningManager.update_task` | ✅ `planning/events.jsonl` line with `action="completed"` |
| `project_manager(action="update_task")` → `ChatManager.update_chat_metadata` | ❌ tool docstring says it records a `ChatStatusEvent`; it does **not** write to `PlanningEventStore` |
| `ChatEngine` run that flips status internally | ❌ nothing |
| `ChatManager.save_chat` (every save) | ⚠️ only an **ephemeral** `chat_event(event_type="changed")` over Socket.IO |

So the orchestrator would miss completions performed by its own PM tool or by any engine run, and would lose everything on restart. **The feature forces a single source of truth**: every status transition must emit the same planning event. That is a pre-existing inconsistency the dashboard activity feed also suffers from, so it is worth fixing regardless — but it is **work this feature cannot avoid**.

### C4 — No concurrency guard on a chat *(high)*

- `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.register(chat.doc_id)` returns a **new** token per call and `finally` unregisters — a second concurrent run of the same chat replaces the token, and the first run’s `finally` clears the second’s. Cancellation becomes unreliable precisely when the loop makes concurrency likely.
- `ChatManager.store_chat` is a full-file rewrite (`json.dumps(chat.model_dump())`). Two writers ⇒ lost updates. The orchestrator plus the background scanner plus a user typing is already three.
- `_BACKGROUND_TASKS` (fire-and-forget in `project_manager._action_request_changes`) is a **module-level set in one process** — a restart drops queued work with no record.

A per-chat lock plus an “in flight” marker is mandatory, not optional.

### C5 — Self-amplification *(high)*

The loop feeds itself unless three things are excluded:

1. the orchestrator’s **own** completion,
2. completions **older** than the last report (watermark),
3. tasks the orchestrator itself just created (`project_manager.create_task` → later completion → next invocation).

`max_agent_iterations` (default 4) bounds the in-turn agent recursion only. It does **not** bound an inter-turn loop. Without a watermark + coalescing + a run budget (`runs`, `max_runs_per_hour`, `estimation_cost`), this is an unbounded token burner — and the failure mode is *silent*, because nobody is watching a background report.

### C6 — No user in a background run *(medium)*

`project_manager` resolves context through `settings._active_session` and `session._current_chat` — stamps written by the AI runtime (`self.settings._active_session = self.session`). In a background thread there may be none, so:

- `_resolve_processing_session` falls back to `CODXJuniorSession(settings=settings)` with `user=None`;
- `_username()` → `None` ⇒ analytics records `"anonymous"` (`_record_chat_session_start`), and created tasks lose the actor;
- two orchestrators (or an orchestrator + a user turn) on the same project settings object can see each other’s session — the shared-mutable hazard from the previous review is **unchanged and now more likely**.

### C7 — Nested engine execution *(medium)*

The orchestrator driving other tasks means `chat_with_project` inside `chat_with_project`. Each nested run creates its own `AgentRunContext`, its own cancellation token, and stamps the shared `_active_session`. Running several tasks in parallel from one orchestrator compounds C3 and C6. Sequential execution is the safe default.

### C8 — “Report as a single document” is not free *(medium)*

The engine always **appends** a response message. Invoked N times, an orchestrator produces N reports unless it explicitly overwrites one (reusing `Message.doc_id` + `update_message`) or leans on `_hide_non_answer_messages` + `is_answer`. That is a deliberate data-model decision, not a side effect — and it determines whether the chat is a “report document” or a “log of reports”.

### C9 — Planning semantics don’t fit liveness *(low/medium)*

- `STATUS_ORDER = ["todo","doing","onhold","done","rejected"]` — no *paused*, *running*, *failed*. Loop state must live elsewhere (see C2).
- A human setting the orchestrator to `done` via the planning UI is a legitimate action that the loop must interpret (stop? keep reporting?). Currently undefined.
- `project_manager.create_task` hardcodes `mode=DEFAULT_MODE` (`"task"`), so the PM tool cannot **create** an orchestrator — it must come from the UI/API. Minor, but it shapes the onboarding flow.
- Uniqueness is enforced by nothing: “one task acts as PM” is a convention. Two orchestrators on the same sprint will both react to the same completion.

### C10 — Event delivery to the UI is best-effort *(low)*

`SessionChannel.send_event` appends to a module-level `EVENT_QUEUE` drained by a thread that either `sio.emit`s or relays through `sio_background` when `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` is set; failures are `logger.error` only. Orchestrator progress in the background process is therefore best-effort — acceptable, but the UI must not be the source of truth for “did it run”.

---

## 6. Trigger source — options

| Source | Durable | Covers all writers | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. `planning/events.jsonl` + watermark** | ✅ | ❌ today (only planning PATCH) | cheap (tail a file) | Ordered, has actor/time. Best record — **once C3 is fixed** |
| **B. Scan chat files by mtime** (`chat_manager.find_chats(last_update)`) | ✅ | ✅ | cheap-ish | Covers any writer; needs previous-state memory and a definition of “finished”; robust as a reconciliation sweep |
| **C. Hook in `save_chat` / PM tool / engine** | ❌ (in-process) | ✅ | free | Immediate and precise, but lost on restart; fires on *every* save (noise) |
| **D. Socket.IO broadcast** | ❌ | ⚠️ | free | UI-centric; no durability |

**Recommended shape:** write with **C**, record with **A**, reconcile with **B**. Concretely: route `project_manager.update_task` (and any engine-driven status change) through the same code path that emits the planning event; the orchestrator tails `events.jsonl` with a watermark stored in its own `loop` block; a periodic sweep catches anything that bypassed the writer. This also fixes the dashboard activity feed gap — a win independent of this feature.

---

## 7. Recommended consolidation

```
mode = "orchestrator"        # identity: behaves as PM, sections the prompt
loop = {                     # lifecycle: may it be re-invoked?
  enabled: bool = False      # the pause switch (checked BEFORE any token spend)
  paused_reason: str | None
  watermark: str | None      # last processed completion event id/timestamp
  runs: int = 0
  last_run_at: str | None
  max_runs_per_hour: int
}
```

- Pause = `loop.enabled = False` (UI toggle, no mode churn, no comment parsing).
- The “pause the loop” **comment** can still be supported by having the tool set `loop.enabled = False` — best of both: human-visible in the conversation, machine-checkable, and durable.
- Coalesce: invoke only when the sprint is **quiescent** (no `doing` tasks) for a short interval, or batch completions into one invocation — otherwise N completions ⇒ N orchestrator runs.

---

## 8. Change surface (only if the design is approved)

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `codx/junior/db.py` | `Chat.loop` block (defaults, disabled) | The pause switch, without overloading `mode` |
| `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` | Reuse `update_task` for all status transitions; add a “completions since watermark” reader | Single durable source of truth (fixes C3) |
| `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | Route `update_task` through the planning writer; let the tool set `loop.enabled=False` on pause | Closes the silent gap; makes pause durable |
| `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `is_orchestrator` in `_resolve_chat_mode_flags`; single-report handling (`is_answer` + `_hide_non_answer_messages`) | Behaviour + “document” semantics |
| `codx/junior/orchestrator.py` **(new)** | Scan → decide (uniqueness, watermark, coalescing, budget, lock) → invoke | No scheduler logic exists anywhere today |
| `codx/junior/background.py` | `check_orchestrators` loop in its own thread, reusing the quarantine/backoff pattern | Restart-resilient host |
| `codx/junior/api/chat.py` | **nothing** | `mode` already round-trips — the concrete payoff of this design |

---

## 9. Open questions (blocking a precise implementation)

1. **Uniqueness:** one orchestrator per board, per sprint, per project — and what wins if two exist (lowest `sort_index`? explicit flag? refuse and report)?
2. **Completion definition:** `status == done` only, `done + rejected`, or any move into a given column?
3. **Coalescing:** run per completion, or once the sprint is quiescent for N seconds?
4. **Authority:** may the orchestrator write (create/assign/move tasks, run `request_changes`), or is it read-only reporting?
5. **Budget:** `Chat.estimation_cost`, a per-orchestrator `max_runs_per_hour`, or project-level?
6. **Report model:** overwrite one `is_answer` message (document) or append per run and hide the rest (log)?
7. **Nested runs:** sequential (safe) or parallel (C6/C7 risk)?
8. **Pause UX:** UI toggle, tool-driven comment, or both (§7 allows both)?

Important: We already have "agent" mode, let's use it.
Agent tasks will be informed when any child task is done (on any nested level)

## open questions answers
1. uniqueness: can be many agent tasks in a board. We must walk up the tree to find the first "agent" task.
2. Completion definition: status == done
3. run per completion
4. Agent will always instructs the tasks to do the work, ensuring they have the right profiles
5. Budget: Agent task has the total budget, already implemented
6. agent tasks will work as "task" mode, generating new report and hidding previous message
7. Nested runs: parallel
8. Pause: Don't re-run agent if last visible message.message_type != 'pause_loop'

I'll verify the existing pieces this design depends on before reviewing: `Message` fields (`message_type`/`is_answer`), agent-mode handling, planning events, and where nested task runs are spawned.Search results are noisy. Reading the authoritative files directly.Key finding already: `Message` has no `message_type` field. Let me verify the tool layer and the task-completion write paths.The tools module path differs. Locating it.`project_manager_tools.py` does not exist. Confirming the actual tool inventory and the parts of the engine I still need (`is_answer`, `save_chat`/status history, background loop).Now reading the actual project-manager tooling and the tool model.Two last verifications: `update_chat_metadata` (status history / event source) and the agent runtime's tool/budget injection.# Review — orchestrator = `agent` mode (no new chat context)

No files modified. Every claim below is anchored in the current code.

---

## 1. What changed vs. the previous design

| Previous | Now | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| New `ChatContext` / `ChatWithContext`, threading through 8 files | **`Chat.mode == "agent"`** — already persisted, already round-tripped by `api_chat` → `Chat(**data)` | −1 model module, −8 files of plumbing, −all transport/compat open questions |
| Completion signal needs a fix (only `/api/planning` PATCH wrote events) | **`Chat.status_history` already exists and is writer-agnostic** (§3) | **Zero changes to write paths** — the biggest win |
| Pause = new field / comment / mode change | Pause = a chat message | No schema change, but the field named does not exist (§5) |

This design is materially smaller than the two prior proposals. Adopt it.

---

## 2. Answer 1 — "walk up to find the first agent task"

**Supported by the code, but two implementation hazards.**

- The parent chain is `Chat.parent_id`; both real sub-task creators set it (`chat_engine_actions.generate_tasks` → `sub_task.parent_id = chat.id`; `project_manager._action_create_task` → `parent_id or (current_chat.id …)`).
- `ChatEngine.get_chat_analysis_parents` and `ChatPromptBuilder.build_parent_message_history` already walk the chain — mirror that pattern.

Hazards to design around:

1. **Cost of the walk.** `ChatManager.find_by_id` scans *every* chat file: `next(path for path in self.chat_paths() if chat_id in path)`. Walking N ancestors = N full directory scans. The scheduler must build an in-memory `{id: chat}` index from one `list_chats()` pass, not call `find_by_id` per hop.
2. **No cycle guard.** Existing walkers (`while parent_chat:`) loop forever on a self/cyclic `parent_id` (reachable via `/api/chats/metadata`, since `update_chat_metadata` `setattr`s any attribute). The new walker needs a visited-set.
3. **Cross-project parents.** `parent_owner_project_id` / `parent_project_id` exist because the parent may live in another project. Use `ChatManager(settings=find_project_by_id(parent_owner_project_id))`, like `_resolve_owner_manager` and `get_chat_manager(project_id=chat.owner_project_id)` already do.

**Cascade (resolves the "first agent" vs "any nested level" tension):** notify only the **nearest** agent ancestor. That agent, when it finishes, is itself a completed child of *its* agent ancestor, so the notification cascades upward naturally. One rule, no fan-out.

```
child(done) → nearest ancestor with mode=="agent" → runs → (if it has an agent ancestor) → that one runs
```

---

## 3. Answer 2 — completion = `status == "done"` → **the signal already exists**

`ChatManager.save_chat` calls `_register_status_change`, which appends a `ChatStatusEvent` to **`Chat.status_history`** whenever `status` actually changes (`from_status`/`to_status`/`user`/`at`), merge-safe by `doc_id`, persisted in the chat JSON.

Who writes `status`, and all of them funnel through `save_chat`:

| Writer | Path | Recorded? |
|---|---|---|
| UI: `PATCH /api/planning/tasks/{id}` | `PlanningManager.update_task` → `setattr` → `save_chat(chat_only=True)` | ✅ |
| AI: `project_manager(action="update_task", status="done")` | `update_chat_metadata` → `save_chat(chat_only=True)` | ✅ |
| Any engine-driven change | `save_chat` | ✅ |

**This supersedes my earlier claim that `planning/events.jsonl` was the only durable record.** `events.jsonl` is still useful for the dashboard feed, but it is *not* needed here: `status_history` covers every writer with no change to any write path. `DONE_STATUSES = {"done"}` in `planning_manager` gives the canonical predicate.

**Watermark without new state.** Do not persist a cursor on the orchestrator. Compare each descendant's latest `to_status == "done"` event `at` against the timestamp of the orchestrator's last visible message. Stateless, restart-safe, no schema change.

> Caveat: `ChatManager.load_chat_from_path(chat_only=True)` truncates `messages` to the last one, and `list_chats()` uses it. That is enough for status scanning but **not** for the pause check or watermark — those need the full chat.

---

## 4. Answer 6 — "agent works as task: new report, hide previous" → **two concrete gaps**

`ChatEngine._hide_non_answer_messages` is applied here:

```python
if _is_refine(chat_mode) or is_vibe:
    self._hide_non_answer_messages(chat=chat)
```

and `_is_refine(mode)` = `mode in ["task", "tutorial"]`. So:

**Gap 1 — agent is excluded.** The orchestrator must join that branch. But applying it to *every* `agent` chat changes the behaviour of all existing agent chats — gate it on the orchestrator condition (§7), not on `mode` alone.

**Gap 2 — nothing ever sets `is_answer = True`.** Verified: `is_answer` is only ever *read* (`_hide_non_answer_messages`, `build_message_history(only_answers=…)`, `append_refine_message`, `is_answer_parent_message`). No engine path writes it. And `build_message_history` is called with `only_answers=(is_refine or is_vibe)`.

Consequence for the orchestrator's "single document": if no message is `is_answer`, history is empty on the next run → the report is not carried forward → the chat is a *log*, not a *document*. So the orchestrator run **must stamp `response_message.is_answer = True`** (and keep the previous report as the document body). That single line is the difference between the two behaviours the user described.

---

## 5. Answer 8 — pause: the field does not exist, and the predicate is inverted

- **`Message` has no `message_type`.** Fields are `role`, `task_item`, `is_answer`, `hide`, `improvement`, `done`, `meta_data`, … The nearest existing concept is **`task_item`**, which already carries non-role semantics: `task_item="status"` (`generate_tasks`) and `MessageTaskItem.SUMMARY`.
- **The predicate as written is backwards.** "Don't re-run agent if last visible message.message_type != 'pause_loop'" would mean *run only when the pause marker is present*. The intended rule is: **do not re-run when the last visible message is the pause marker.**

Proposed (no schema change):

```
paused  ⇔  task_item == "pause_loop"   on the last message with hide == False
```

Notes that matter for correctness:
- Must read the **full** chat (`find_by_id`), not `list_chats()` (which keeps only the last message).
- Must filter `hide`/`improvement`, and skip the streaming/tool scaffolding messages the bridge appends mid-run, otherwise "last message" is the assistant's own output.
- `task_item` is a free `str`, so a new value needs no migration; a UI that renders unknown `task_item` values must be checked.
- If a hard boolean is preferred later, `Message.meta_data["loop_paused"]` works too — but `task_item` keeps the marker visible in the transcript, which is the user's stated intent.

---

## 6. Answers 3, 5, 7 — loop mechanics and the real risks

**Answer 5 — budget is genuinely already implemented.** `Chat.estimation_cost` + monotonic `Chat.cost` (accumulated in `ChatManager._accumulate_message_cost`, never decreased by deletes), consumed by SmolAgent to stop over-budget chats. Two consequences for a forever-loop:
- An orchestrator accumulating cost for weeks will eventually hit `estimation_cost` and **stop silently**. That is a good natural circuit-breaker, but it must be *reported* (a message/event), not discovered by absence of reports.
- The budget is on the orchestrator only; child runs are charged to the child chats, so the orchestrator's `cost` does not reflect the work it caused. Confirm that is intended.

**Answer 3 (run per completion) + Answer 7 (parallel) = the highest-risk combination.** Three concrete, pre-existing defects that a loop makes likely:

| Defect | Where | Why the loop triggers it |
|---|---|---|
| **Cancellation token collision** | `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.register(chat.doc_id)` returns a **new** token per call; `finally` unregisters | Two concurrent runs of the same orchestrator replace each other's token; the first `finally` clears the second's → cancellation unreliable exactly when concurrency is expected |
| **Lost updates on save** | `ChatManager.store_chat` = full-file `json.dumps(chat.model_dump())` rewrite | Orchestrator + scheduler + a human typing = 3 writers, last-writer-wins |
| **Shared mutable context stamps** | `settings._active_session`, `session._current_chat` — read by `project_manager._resolve_chat_session`, `_current_chat`, `_username` | Parallel child runs on the same project settings object see each other's session/chat → wrong parent_id, wrong actor, wrong chat |

The third one is the direct blocker for answer 7: `project_manager` resolves *everything* through `settings._active_session` and `session._current_chat`. Parallel `request_changes` on the same settings instance is unsafe until that resolution becomes explicit (context var / passed parameter) instead of an object stamp.

Also, "run per completion" with N parallel completions = N orchestrator runs. Minimum mitigation: **dedupe by `(task_id, status_event.doc_id)` watermark** + **a per-orchestrator in-flight lock**. `_BACKGROUND_TASKS` (a module-level `set` in `project_manager`) is the existing precedent — process-local, lost on restart. Acceptable for v1 only if the watermark makes a lost run self-healing (it does, because the status event persists).

**Answer 4 (agent instructs the tasks).** `project_manager(action="request_changes", chat_id=…, comment=…, profiles=[…])` exists and works: the comment is appended, `save_chat` recomputes `chat.profiles` from message profiles, and the child is processed. Gap: the tool has **no sprints/board inheritance and no orchestrator awareness** — the orchestrator must pass `chat_id` explicitly, which means it first needs to list its children (`list_tasks` filters by board/column/sprint only, **not by parent**). A `parent_id` filter on `list_tasks` is the missing primitive.

**Answer 1 corollary.** `_action_create_task` hardcodes `mode=DEFAULT_MODE` (`"task"`), and `create_task_tool` likewise sets `mode="task"`. So the AI can never create an orchestrator — only a human/UI can. That is the right default; state it explicitly.

---

## 7. The design's main weakness: `mode` is overloaded again

`mode="agent"` today means **"iterate within the turn until `AGENT_DONE_WORD`"** (`_resolve_chat_mode_flags` → `is_agent` → `append_agent_message` + the step-24 recursion, bounded by `max_agent_iterations` = 4).

The orchestrator adds a second, orthogonal meaning: **"may be re-invoked when a descendant completes"** — an inter-turn lifecycle property.

If the trigger keys on `mode == "agent"` alone, **every agent chat in every project becomes a polling target**, and any `estimation_cost`-bearing agent chat starts burning tokens unattended. That is the single largest regression risk in this proposal — larger than the earlier `ChatContext` plumbing risk it removes.

Recommendation: keep `mode="agent"` as the behaviour (in-turn iteration + report semantics) and add an explicit, cheap **gate** that the scheduler checks before any token spend. Cheapest options, no new Chat model field:

| Gate | Where it already lives | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `mode == "agent"` **and** `chat.status` is a live state (`todo`/`doing`) | `Chat.status` | zero schema change; also gives "stopping = set it done" |
| `mode == "agent"` **and** `"orchestrator" in (chat.tags or [])` | `Chat.tags` (already used by planning) | zero schema change, explicit, UI-editable |
| `mode == "agent"` **and** `chat.parent_id is None` | existing field | weakest — most agent chats are rootless |

`chat.status in ACTIVE_STATUSES` is attractive: it reuses `planning_manager.ACTIVE_STATUSES`, and it makes answer #2 self-consistent (a `done` orchestrator stops, a `todo`/`doing` one loops). Combined with the pause marker, it gives two independent stop switches with no new fields.

---

## 8. Pros & cons

### Pros

1. **No transport, no persistence, no tool-plumbing work.** `api_chat`, `SioChatMessage`, `session`/`engine` signatures, `ai.py`, `smol_agent`, `ToolSettings` — all untouched. `mode` already round-trips.
2. **The completion signal is free and writer-agnostic** (`Chat.status_history`), unlike `planning/events.jsonl`. Both the UI and the AI tool already record transitions, and both already go through `save_chat`.
3. **A task *is* a chat.** `planning_manager._is_task` only excludes `mode=="chat"` without planning signal, so an agent task appears in `query_tasks`, `build_dashboard`, `board_progress`, attention and metrics with zero query changes.
4. **Instructions + profiles are already user-defined** (`Chat.profiles` → `_resolve_profiles_and_model`, recursive linked profiles, per-profile `tools`/`llm_model`/`guardrails`). `project_manager` is registered in `TOOLS` with `session: True`, `project_settings: True`, `dual_response: True`.
5. **Budget exists** (`estimation_cost`/`cost`), **cost is observable** (`Message.cost`/`cost_info`), **analytics already records `mode`** per session.
6. **A background host exists**, with quarantine/backoff and restart tolerance (`background.check_projects`, `MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS`, `QUARANTINE_DELAYS`). A third `check_orchestrators` thread follows an established pattern.
7. **Parallel sub-task execution already exists** (`generate_tasks` → `asyncio.gather`), so answer #7 is consistent with the codebase's precedent — for *distinct* chats.
8. **One branch point.** `_resolve_chat_mode_flags` is the natural home for `is_orchestrator`, keeping `_chat_with_project_inner` readable.

### Cons

1. **`mode` overloaded** (§7) — highest risk; the trigger must have a second gate or every agent chat becomes a loop.
2. **The pause field does not exist** (§5) — `message_type` is not a `Message` field; `task_item` is the real one, and the stated predicate is inverted.
3. **`is_answer` is never set by the engine** (§4) — without stamping it, the "single report document" degrades to a log and the next run loses the report entirely.
4. **Concurrency is not safe today** for parallel runs on the same project settings (§6): shared `_active_session`/`_current_chat`, token collision, full-file rewrites.
5. **Run-per-completion amplifies cost** and, with answer #7, multiplication across levels. Requires dedupe + in-flight lock + a visible budget stop, none of which exist.
6. **Auto-generated sub-tasks inherit `parent_id`**, so a *task* created by the AI becomes a descendant of the orchestrator → its completion triggers another run → the orchestrator reacts to work it itself ordered. Expected, but it must be bounded (in-flight lock + budget), and the report should distinguish "completed by me" from "completed by a human".
7. **`list_tasks` cannot filter by `parent_id`** — the orchestrator has no way to enumerate its own children with the current tool surface.
8. **`find_by_id` is a full-tree scan** per call; a per-3s scheduler doing ancestor walks is O(files) each cycle. Needs one index pass per cycle.
9. **Agent prompt is task-shaped**: `append_agent_message` says *"You are responsible to end this task… Return `AGENT_DONE_WORD`"* and passes `<task>{chat.name}</task>`. An orchestrator needs different framing (report + delegate + pause), so the prompt must branch or the orchestrator profile must override it.
10. **No uniqueness** by design (many agents per board) → the same descendant can be claimed by two ancestors only if the tree is malformed; the nearest-ancestor rule makes that impossible, but a visited-set is still required.

---

## 9. Behaviour matrix (agreed answers applied)

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `mode != "agent"` | untouched, byte-for-byte today's behaviour |
| agent chat, gate not satisfied (§7) | untouched; **no scheduler entry** |
| agent on a board, descendant reaches `status == "done"` | nearest agent ancestor is invoked once per `ChatStatusEvent` |
| … while that ancestor is already running | skipped (in-flight lock); the event remains detectable → self-healing next cycle |
| … more nested levels | cascades upward one level at a time (nearest first) |
| last visible message has `task_item == "pause_loop"` | not invoked; manual invocation still works |
| `status == "done"` on the orchestrator itself | not invoked (drops out of `ACTIVE_STATUSES`) |
| `Chat.cost >= estimation_cost` | SmolAgent stops; the stop **must** be surfaced in the chat |
| descendant completion older than the last report | ignored (stateless watermark) |
| `generate_tasks` / `project_manager.create_task` children | inherit `parent_id`, therefore participate — bounded by lock + budget |

---

## 10. Remaining open questions (3, down from 8)

1. **Gate for the trigger** (§7): `status in ACTIVE_STATUSES`, `"orchestrator" in chat.tags`, or an explicit new field? (Recommend status — zero schema and it makes "done = stop" consistent with answer #2.)
2. **Pause marker**: `task_item = "pause_loop"` on a `user` message (visible, no schema) — accepted? And confirm the predicate is "pause **when present**", not as literally written.
3. **Report document**: is stamping `is_answer = True` on the orchestrator's response the agreed mechanism for "single document" (with `_hide_non_answer_messages` applied to the orchestrator)? If the client already sets `is_answer`, this becomes a verification instead of a change.

---

## 11. Implementation order (only after Q1–Q3)

| # | File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `codx/junior/orchestrator.py` **(new)** | one index pass per cycle → `{id: chat}`; nearest-agent-ancestor resolver (visited-set, cross-project aware); `status_history` watermark vs. last report time; pause check on the full chat; in-flight lock; dedupe by `(task_id, event.doc_id)` | No scheduler logic exists anywhere; keeps it testable and out of the engine |
| 2 | `codx/junior/background.py` | `check_orchestrators` thread next to `check_projects`, honouring `RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` + `QUARANTINE_*` | Restart-resilient host already exists |
| 3 | `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` | `is_orchestrator` inside `_resolve_chat_mode_flags`; include it in the `_hide_non_answer_messages` branch; stamp `is_answer = True`; orchestrator prompt framing | Behaviour + "report document" semantics |
| 4 | `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | `parent_id` filter on `list_tasks`; optional `task_item`/`pause` support so the AI can pause itself | The orchestrator needs to see its children |
| 5 | `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` or `chat_engine.py` | make the budget stop visible in the chat | Silent stop is the worst failure mode for an unattended loop |
| 6 | *(deferred)* explicit run context replacing `settings._active_session` / `session._current_chat` | makes answer #7 (parallel) genuinely safe | Largest refactor; not required for a sequential v1 |

Steps 1–3 deliver the feature; 4–5 make it usable unattended; 6 is the debt this design defers.
