"""
Prompt and message construction for chat interactions.

Extracted from ``ChatEngine`` to keep prompt-building logic (history
rendering, refine/agent prompts, current-request wrapping, and response file
extraction) in one place and reduce the size of the engine module.

The key idea is to demote prior conversation turns to inert *context* so the
model does not re-execute instructions that were already processed:

* Prior turns are wrapped in a ``<conversation_history>`` block and their
  assistant messages are labelled ``<assistant_done>``.
* The live instruction is isolated in a ``<current_request>`` block.

Multimodal content
------------------
Messages with attachments are converted into LangChain messages whose
``content`` is a LIST of parts (``{"type": "text"}`` plus one
``{"type": "image_url"}`` per image). Prompt assembly must therefore only
ever rewrite the TEXT part: stringifying the list would replace the images
with their Python representation and make them invisible to the model.
See :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._get_text_content` /
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._set_text_content`.

Conversation attachments
------------------------
``Message.attachments`` must ALWAYS be visible to the model — not only on the
message that happens to be the current request. Because the history block is
rendered as plain text, images carried by prior turns would otherwise be lost.

:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.collect_attachments` gathers the attachments of EVERY
visible message (parent chats first, then the current chat) and
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_ai_prompt_messages` appends them to the single
``<current_request>`` message:

* ``image/*`` attachments become ``{"type": "image_url"}`` parts,
* every other type (audio notes, documents) is listed in a ``## Attachments``
  text block ONLY, so the model still knows it exists without the request
  carrying an invalid ``image_url`` part.

Attachment payload normalization
--------------------------------
An ``image_url`` part is only useful when the provider can DECODE it. When it
cannot, models do not fail the request: they replace the image with an
``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder, which looks like "the AI cannot see my
screenshots". :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._prepare_attachment` therefore
normalizes every payload before it is sent:

* a ``base64_data`` value that already holds a full ``data:`` URI is not
  prefixed a second time (``data:image/png;base64,data:image/png;base64,...``
  is not decodable),
* whitespace/newlines inside the base64 payload are stripped,
* the media type is resolved from ``file_type`` → data-URI header → file
  extension, so ``application/octet-stream`` / ``image/*`` are never sent,
* only formats vision APIs accept (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF) travel as parts —
  SVG/BMP/TIFF/HEIC are listed in the text block instead,
* oversized screenshots are downscaled/re-encoded (Pillow, best effort,
  cached per payload).

The resulting status of every attachment (mime, size, sent / not sent and
why) is written into the ``## Attachments`` text block.
"""

"""
Project manager tools for codx-junior.

These tools let a profile (AI role) act as a **project manager** over the
project's kanban tasks (each task is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in
``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/``). They cover the day-to-day workflow:

    - ``create_task``     : create a new task chat associated to a kanban
                            board + column and one or more sprints.
    - ``get_task``        : review a task (status, board/column, sprints and
                            the visible conversation).
    - ``list_tasks``      : list/filter tasks (board, column, sprint, status,
                            free-text).
    - ``list_boards``     : discover the kanban boards, their columns, the
                            sprint boards and the valid task states (so names
                            are known before creating or moving a task).
    - ``update_task``     : change the task status and/or move it between
                            boards, columns and sprints (and edit priority,
                            due date, progress, assignees and tags).
    - ``request_changes`` : add a comment **and** process the task through
                            :class:`~codx.junior.chat.chat_engine.ChatEngine`
                            (``session.chat_with_project``).
    - ``request_help``    : add a comment **without** triggering the engine
                            (ask the user for help / leave a note).

Design notes:
    - **One tool, several actions.** Keeping the workflow unified (like
      ``team_management``/``profile_management``) avoids spending prompt tokens
      on a schema per action and keeps the mental model small.
    - **Nothing duplicated.** Tasks are plain chats: this module never
      re-implements persistence, it delegates to
      :class:`~codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager`
      (``save_chat`` / ``update_chat_metadata`` / ``find_by_id`` / ``list_chats``).
      ``update_chat_metadata`` keeps messages intact and records a
      ``ChatStatusEvent`` on every real status transition, so task-performance
      metrics keep working.
    - **Processing is explicit.** Only ``request_changes`` runs the engine;
      ``request_help`` only writes a comment. A background run preserves the
      coroutine reference so it is not garbage-collected.
    - **Strict destination validation.** A task can NEVER be stored on a board,
      a column, a sprint or a state that does not exist: those values are
      validated against the project catalogue (``tasks/kanban.json`` and the
      states owned by :mod:`codx.junior.planning_manager`) and an invalid value
      is rejected with an error that lists the available options and asks to
      create the missing one first. The catalogue spelling is also enforced, so
      ``bugs`` resolves to the existing ``Bugs`` board instead of creating a
      phantom ``.codx/tasks/bugs`` folder.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

This lets the whole feature live in **three files** (one new), with no changes to `api/chat.py`, `chat_engine.py`, `sio`, or the `Chat` model.

## Change proposal

1. **`globals.py`** — canonical constants (`agent` mode, `pause_loop`, `resume_loop`, `agent_trigger`).
2. **`agent_orchestrator.py` (new)** — detection (index → done → nearest agent ancestor → pause → watermark → budget/backoff/in-flight) and execution (trigger message → `ChatEngine` run with the orchestrator system prompt → collapse to a single report).
3. **`background.py`** — `check_agent_tasks` thread, pool per project (parallel across projects, sequential within one — parallel agents of the same project share `settings._active_session`).

|---|---|---|
| `codx/junior/globals.py` | +4 constants | Single source for the markers, importable by every layer without cycles |
| `codx/junior/agent_orchestrator.py` **(new)** | `AgentOrchestrator`, `AgentTrigger`, `is_loop_paused`, `last_completed_at`, in-flight lock, failure backoff | The feature; no engine plumbing |

"""
Agent orchestrator: keeps ``agent`` mode tasks working as project managers.

An **agent task** is a regular task (chat) whose ``mode`` is ``agent``
(:data:`codx.junior.globals.CHAT_MODE_AGENT`). It acts as the project manager of
the board/sprint it lives on: it keeps a single report document and delegates
the real work to other tasks. Instructions and profiles come from the chat and
from the profiles, exactly like any other task, and the budget is the existing
``Chat.estimation_cost`` / ``Chat.cost`` pair.

This module makes it *live*: every time a task reaches the ``done`` status — at
any nesting level — the **nearest agent ancestor** of that task is re-invoked so
it can update its report and delegate the next steps.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[cycle: one index pass per project] --> B[chats with status done]
    B --> C[walk up parent_id chain - visited set]
    C -->|no agent ancestor| Z[ignore]
    C -->|agent ancestor| D{agent live?}
    D -->|done / rejected| Z
    D -->|yes| E{loop paused?}
    E -->|newest loop marker is pause_loop| Z
    E -->|no| F{completion newer than last report?}
    F -->|no| Z
    F -->|yes| G{budget / backoff / in flight?}
    G -->|yes| Z
    G -->|no| H[append agent_trigger message]
    H --> I[run the agent through ChatEngine]
    I --> J{single report produced?}
    J -->|no| K[hide the trigger - retry next cycle]
    J -->|yes| L[collapse to a single report document]
    L --> M[watermark advances - the report timestamp]
```

Design notes
------------
* **The completion signal already exists.** ``Chat.status_history`` is appended
  by :meth:`codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager.save_chat` whenever ``status``
  actually changes, whichever writer did it (planning PATCH, the
  ``project_manager`` tool, an engine run). No write path is modified.
* **Stateless watermark.** The trigger is "a completion newer than the agent's
  last visible message". No cursor is persisted, so a restart, a crash or a lost
  in-flight run self-heals on the next cycle.
* **Nearest ancestor only.** Notifying the nearest agent ancestor cascades
  naturally: when that agent finishes, its own completion notifies *its* agent
  ancestor. There is no fan-out, so a task can never be claimed twice.
* **Pause is a message, not a setting.** The loop is paused when the newest loop
  marker of the agent is
  :data:`~codx.junior.globals.TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP`; a human message or
  :data:`~codx.junior.globals.TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP` resumes it. Because the
  engine only skips *hidden* messages when walking back, an assistant reply that
  follows the pause marker does not resume the loop.
* **One report document.** After a run every message but the new report is
  hidden (and the report is flagged ``is_answer``), so the chat is a document
  that is replaced on every run and the history loaded by the next run is the
  report itself.
* **Bounded cost.** Three independent guards: the chat budget
  (``estimation_cost``, enforced by SmolAgent), an in-process in-flight lock and
  an exponential failure backoff. Runaway loops are also structurally unlikely:
  with no new completion there is no run.
* **Sequential within a project.** Agent runs of the same project share the
  project settings object, which SmolAgent stamps with
  ``_active_session`` / ``_current_chat``; running them in parallel would let
  them resolve each other's chat. Projects ARE processed in parallel by
  :func:`codx.junior.background.check_agent_tasks`.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from threading import Lock
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager, _parse_timestamp
from codx.junior.db import Chat, Message
from codx.junior.globals import (
    CHAT_MODE_AGENT,
    TASK_ITEM_AGENT_TRIGGER,
    TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP,
    TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP,
)
from codx.junior.planning_manager import CLOSED_STATUSES, DONE_STATUSES
from codx.junior.project.project_discover import find_project_by_id

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: System prompt that turns the run into a project-manager run. It is passed
#: through ``ChatEngine.chat_with_project(system=...)`` so it participates in
#: every iteration of the agent without touching the prompt builder.
ORCHESTRATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
AGENT ORCHESTRATOR ROLE
You are the project manager (orchestrator) of a task board. This task IS the
plan: a single report document that states where the work stands and delegates
what must happen next. You are re-invoked automatically every time one of your
tasks reaches the "done" status, and your answer replaces the previous report.

HOW TO WORK
1. Inspect your tasks with the `project_manager` tool before deciding anything:
   `action="list_tasks"` (filter by board/column/sprint/status/query) and
   `action="get_task"` to read one. The tasks you own are the descendants of
   this task.
2. Delegate, never implement. Order work with `action="create_task"` (name and
   description are mandatory) or `action="request_changes"` (adds a comment and
   processes the task). Always provide the `profiles` of the role that must do
   the work; they are never inherited.
3. Keep the board honest with `action="update_task"` (status, priority,
   assignees, sprint, progress).
4. Answer with ONE report: what is done, what is in progress, what is next and
   what you need from a human. It must be self-contained, because it replaces
   the previous report and is the only history kept.
5. Never report work as pending when a task is already done, and never order
   the same work twice.
"""

#: Chats currently being re-invoked by this process. Guards against a second
#: cycle invoking the same agent while the first run is still in flight.
_RUNNING: Set[str] = set()
_RUNNING_LOCK = Lock()

#: Consecutive failures per agent, used to stop spending tokens on a broken
#: agent. Delay (in seconds) is indexed by the failure count.
_FAILURES: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
FAILURE_DELAYS: List[int] = [0, 60, 300, 900, 3600]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _normalize(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Lower-case and strip a chat/message field (``None`` becomes ``""``)."""
    return (value or "").strip().lower()


def _parse(value: Optional[str]) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """Parse a timestamp, returning ``None`` instead of ``datetime.min``."""
    parsed = _parse_timestamp(value)
    return None if parsed == datetime.min else parsed


def _is_visible(message: Message) -> bool:
    """Return True when *message* is shown to the user (and to the model)."""
    return not message.hide and not message.improvement


def is_agent_chat(chat: Optional[Chat]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *chat* is an agent (orchestrator) task."""
    return bool(chat) and _normalize(chat.mode) == CHAT_MODE_AGENT


def is_agent_live(chat: Chat) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when the agent loop may still run.

    A closed status (``done`` / ``rejected``) stops the loop, which makes
    "mark the agent as done" a second, independent way to stop it. An empty
    status (new task) is considered live.
    """
    status = _normalize(chat.status)
    return not status or status not in CLOSED_STATUSES


def budget_reached(chat: Chat) -> bool:
    """Return True when the chat already spent its ``estimation_cost``."""
    limit = getattr(chat, "estimation_cost", None)
    if not limit or limit <= 0:
        return False
    return (getattr(chat, "cost", 0.0) or 0.0) >= limit


def is_loop_paused(chat: Chat) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when the agent loop is paused.

    The newest *loop marker* decides. Walking back from the end:

    * :data:`TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP` → paused,
    * :data:`TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP` → running,
    * a real user message (not the synthetic orchestrator trigger) → running
      (implicit resume: someone replied in the chat),
    * anything else (assistant answers, tool scaffolding, hidden messages) is
      skipped.

    This means an assistant answer written *after* the pause marker does not
    resume the loop, while a human reply does.

    :param chat: Full chat (all messages loaded).
    :return: True when the loop is paused.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if message.improvement:
            continue
        task_item = _normalize(message.task_item)
        if task_item == TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP:
            return True
        if task_item == TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP:
            return False
        if message.hide:
            continue
        if not (message.content or "").strip():
            continue
        if message.role == "user" and not (message.meta_data or {}).get("agent_trigger"):
            return False
    return False


def last_visible_at(chat: Chat) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """
    Return the timestamp of the newest visible message of *chat*.

    This is the watermark of the agent: a completion older than this timestamp
    has already been reported.

    :param chat: Full chat (all messages loaded).
    :return: Timestamp, or ``None`` when the chat has no visible message.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if not _is_visible(message):
            continue
        return _parse(message.updated_at) or _parse(message.created_at)
    return None


def last_completed_at(chat: Chat) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """
    Return when *chat* last reached the ``done`` status.

    Uses ``Chat.status_history`` — the append-only, writer-agnostic transition
    log maintained by :class:`~codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager` — so a
    completion performed by the UI, by the ``project_manager`` tool or by an
    engine run is detected exactly the same way.

    :param chat: Chat to inspect (only ``status`` and ``status_history`` are
        needed, so a truncated chat from ``list_chats()`` is enough).
    :return: Timestamp of the newest ``done`` transition, or ``None``.
    """
    stamps = [
        _parse(event.at)
        for event in (chat.status_history or [])
        if _normalize(event.to_status) in DONE_STATUSES
    ]
    stamps = [stamp for stamp in stamps if stamp]
    if stamps:
        return max(stamps)

    # Legacy chats persisted before status_history existed.
    if _normalize(chat.status) in DONE_STATUSES:
        return _parse(chat.updated_at)
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In-flight lock & failure backoff
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _acquire(chat_id: str) -> bool:
    """Mark *chat_id* as running; returns False when it is already running."""
    with _RUNNING_LOCK:
        if chat_id in _RUNNING:
            return False
        _RUNNING.add(chat_id)
        return True


def _release(chat_id: str) -> None:
    """Release the in-flight mark of *chat_id*."""
    with _RUNNING_LOCK:
        _RUNNING.discard(chat_id)


def _in_backoff(chat_id: str) -> bool:
    """Return True while *chat_id* is serving a failure backoff delay."""
    with _RUNNING_LOCK:
        info = _FAILURES.get(chat_id)
        if not info:
            return False
        count = min(info.get("count", 0), len(FAILURE_DELAYS) - 1)
        delay = FAILURE_DELAYS[count]
        if delay <= 0:
            return False
        elapsed = (datetime.now() - info["at"]).total_seconds()
        return elapsed < delay


def _record_failure(chat_id: str) -> None:
    """Register a failed run of *chat_id* (increments the backoff counter)."""
    with _RUNNING_LOCK:
        info = _FAILURES.setdefault(chat_id, {"count": 0, "at": datetime.now()})
        info["count"] = info.get("count", 0) + 1
        info["at"] = datetime.now()
        logger.warning(
            "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' failure #%d registered",
            chat_id,
            info["count"],
        )


def _clear_failure(chat_id: str) -> None:
    """Reset the failure counter of *chat_id* after a successful run."""
    with _RUNNING_LOCK:
        _FAILURES.pop(chat_id, None)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Trigger model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class AgentTrigger:
    """
    One pending agent re-invocation.

    Attributes:
        agent_id: Id of the agent task to re-invoke.
        agent_name: Name of the agent task (for logging/events).
        project_id: Project where the agent task is stored.
        completed: Completed descendant tasks (dicts with ``id``, ``name``,
            ``status``, ``board``, ``column`` and ``completed_at``).
    """
    agent_id: str
    agent_name: str = ""
    project_id: Optional[str] = None
    completed: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Orchestrator
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AgentOrchestrator:
    """
    Detect and re-invoke the agent tasks of a project.

    One instance is meant to be used for a single cycle: it caches the chat
    index per project so the ancestor walk costs one directory scan per
    project instead of one scan per hop
    (:meth:`ChatManager.find_by_id` scans the whole tasks tree).

    :param settings: Settings of the project to process.
    :param session: Optional session override (unused by default; the engine is
        created per run so it never re-enters an in-flight run).
    :param disable_knowledge: Skip the RAG search of the agent runs, making the
        background loop cheaper.

    Example:
        >>> orchestrator = AgentOrchestrator(settings=project)
        >>> triggers = await orchestrator.run_once()
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings,
        session=None,
        disable_knowledge: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self.settings = settings
        self.project_id = getattr(settings, "project_id", None)
        self.session = session
        self.disable_knowledge = disable_knowledge
        self._indexes: Dict[str, Dict[str, Chat]] = {}
        self._managers: Dict[str, Optional[ChatManager]] = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Managers & indexes
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _manager(self, project_id: Optional[str]) -> Optional[ChatManager]:
        """
        Return (and cache) the :class:`ChatManager` of *project_id*.

        :param project_id: Project id (defaults to the orchestrator project).
        :return: The manager, or ``None`` when the project cannot be resolved.
        """
        project_id = project_id or self.project_id
        if project_id in self._managers:
            return self._managers[project_id]

        if project_id == self.project_id:
            project_settings = self.settings
        else:
            project_settings = find_project_by_id(project_id=project_id)

        if project_settings is None:
            logger.warning(
                "agent orchestrator: project '%s' could not be resolved",
                project_id,
            )
            self._managers[project_id] = None
            return None

        manager = ChatManager(settings=project_settings)
        self._managers[project_id] = manager
        return manager

    def _index(self, project_id: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Chat]:
        """
        Return (and cache) the ``{chat_id: chat}`` index of *project_id*.

        Built from a single :meth:`ChatManager.list_chats` pass. The chats are
        truncated to their last message, which is enough for everything the
        detector needs (``mode``, ``status``, ``status_history``, ``parent_id``,
        ``updated_at``). Full chats are loaded only for the candidate agents.

        :param project_id: Project id (defaults to the orchestrator project).
        :return: Mapping of chat id to chat (empty when unavailable).
        """
        project_id = project_id or self.project_id
        if project_id in self._indexes:
            return self._indexes[project_id]

        manager = self._manager(project_id)
        if manager is None:
            self._indexes[project_id] = {}
            return {}

        try:
            chats = manager.list_chats()
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "agent orchestrator: cannot list chats of project '%s': %s",
                project_id,
                ex,
            )
            chats = []

        index = {chat.id: chat for chat in chats if chat.id}
        self._indexes[project_id] = index
        logger.debug(
            "agent orchestrator: indexed %d chat(s) of project '%s'",
            len(index),
            project_id,
        )
        return index

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Ancestor walk
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _parent_chat(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
        project_id: Optional[str],
    ) -> Optional[Tuple[Chat, str]]:
        """
        Resolve the parent of *chat*, crossing project boundaries when needed.

        The parent is looked up in the current project first (the common case:
        a task and its agent live on the same board) and then in the project the
        child declares for its parent (``parent_owner_project_id`` /
        ``parent_project_id``).

        :param chat: Child chat.
        :param project_id: Project where *chat* is stored.
        :return: Tuple of ``(parent_chat, parent_project_id)``, or ``None``.
        """
        parent_id = chat.parent_id
        if not parent_id:
            return None

        candidates: List[str] = []
        for candidate in (
            project_id,
            chat.parent_owner_project_id,
            chat.parent_project_id,
            self.project_id,
        ):
            if candidate and candidate not in candidates:
                candidates.append(candidate)

        for candidate in candidates:
            parent = self._index(candidate).get(parent_id)
            if parent is not None:
                return parent, candidate
        return None

    def _nearest_agent_ancestor(
        self,
        chat: Chat,
    ) -> Tuple[Optional[Chat], Optional[str]]:
        """
        Return the nearest ``agent`` ancestor of *chat*.

        A visited set guards against a malformed (self/cyclic) ``parent_id``
        chain, which would otherwise hang the scheduler.

        :param chat: Child chat.
        :return: Tuple of ``(agent_chat, agent_project_id)``, or ``(None, None)``.
        """
        visited: Set[str] = {chat.id} if chat.id else set()
        current: Optional[Chat] = chat
        current_project_id = self.project_id

        while current is not None:
            parent_info = self._parent_chat(current, current_project_id)
            if parent_info is None:
                return None, None
            parent, parent_project_id = parent_info
            if parent.id in visited:
                logger.warning(
                    "agent orchestrator: parent cycle detected at chat '%s'",
                    parent.id,
                )
                return None, None
            visited.add(parent.id)
            if is_agent_chat(parent):
                return parent, parent_project_id
            current, current_project_id = parent, parent_project_id

        return None, None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Detection
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def collect_triggers(self) -> List[AgentTrigger]:
        """
        Return the agent tasks that must be re-invoked in this cycle.

        For every chat of the project that reached ``done``, the nearest agent
        ancestor is resolved; the trigger is kept only when the agent is live
        (not ``done``/``rejected``), not paused, not over budget, not in failure
        backoff, not already running and the completion is newer than the
        agent's last visible message (the watermark).

        :return: Pending triggers (one per agent, whatever the number of
            completions — a single run reports all of them).
        """
        pending: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}

        for chat in list(self._index(self.project_id).values()):
            completed_at = last_completed_at(chat)
            if completed_at is None:
                continue

            agent, agent_project_id = self._nearest_agent_ancestor(chat)
            if agent is None:
                continue

            entry = pending.setdefault(
                agent.id,
                {
                    "project_id": agent_project_id,
                    "name": agent.name or "",
                    "completed": [],
                },
            )
            entry["completed"].append({
                "id": chat.id,
                "name": chat.name or "",
                "status": chat.status or "",
                "board": chat.board or "",
                "column": chat.column or "",
                "completed_at": completed_at,
            })

        triggers: List[AgentTrigger] = []
        for agent_id, entry in pending.items():
            manager = self._manager(entry["project_id"])
            agent = manager.find_by_id(chat_id=agent_id) if manager else None
            if agent is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' not found in project '%s'",
                    agent_id,
                    entry["project_id"],
                )
                continue

            if not is_agent_live(agent):
                logger.debug(
                    "agent orchestrator: skipping '%s' (closed status '%s')",
                    agent.name,
                    agent.status,
                )
                continue
            if is_loop_paused(agent):
                logger.debug(
                    "agent orchestrator: skipping '%s' (loop paused)",
                    agent.name,
                )
                continue
            if budget_reached(agent):
                logger.info(
                    "agent orchestrator: skipping '%s' (estimation_cost reached: %.6f/%.6f)",
                    agent.name,
                    agent.cost or 0.0,
                    agent.estimation_cost,
                )
                continue
            if _in_backoff(agent_id):
                logger.debug(
                    "agent orchestrator: skipping '%s' (failure backoff)",
                    agent.name,
                )
                continue

            # Watermark: a completion older than the last visible message of the
            # agent has already been reported. Stateless, restart-safe.
            watermark = last_visible_at(agent)
            new_items = [
                item for item in entry["completed"]
                if watermark is None or item["completed_at"] > watermark
            ]
            if not new_items:
                continue

            triggers.append(AgentTrigger(
                agent_id=agent_id,
                agent_name=agent.name or "",
                project_id=entry["project_id"],
                completed=sorted(new_items, key=lambda item: item["completed_at"]),
            ))

        return triggers

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Rendering
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _cell(value: Any) -> str:
        """Render a Markdown table cell (pipes and newlines escaped)."""
        text = str(value if value not in (None, "") else "-")
        return text.replace("|", "/").replace("\n", " ").strip()

    @classmethod
    def _build_trigger_content(cls, trigger: AgentTrigger) -> str:
        """
        Build the content of the trigger message appended to the agent.

        It is a data block only: the instructions live in
        :data:`ORCHESTRATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, so the same text is valid for a
        scheduler trigger and for a human reply.

        :param trigger: The pending trigger.
        :return: Markdown content.
        """
        lines = [
            f"## Tasks completed: {len(trigger.completed)}",
            "",
            "| Task | Status | Board/Column | Finished | Task id |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|",
        ]
        for item in trigger.completed:
            lines.append(
                f"| {cls._cell(item['name'])} | {cls._cell(item['status'])} | "
                f"{cls._cell(item['board'])}/{cls._cell(item['column'])} | "
                f"{item['completed_at'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} | "
                f"`{item['id']}` |"
            )
        lines.extend([
            "",
            "Update your report and delegate the next steps.",
            "If nothing is left to do, say so explicitly in the report.",
        ])
        return "\n".join(lines)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Execution
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _emit(
        manager: Optional[ChatManager],
        chat: Chat,
        message: str,
        event_type: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Emit a chat event, never letting a notification failure break a run."""
        event_manager = getattr(manager, "event_manager", None) if manager else None
        if event_manager is None:
            return
        try:
            if event_type:
                event_manager.chat_event(
                    chat=chat, message=message, event_type=event_type
                )
            else:
                event_manager.chat_event(chat=chat, message=message)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("agent orchestrator: could not emit chat event: %s", ex)

    @staticmethod
    def _collapse_to_single_report(manager: ChatManager, chat: Chat, report: Message) -> None:
        """
        Turn the agent chat into a single report document.

        The new report is flagged ``is_answer`` and every other message is
        hidden, so:

        * the UI shows one document (the report) plus the pending user message,
        * the history loaded by the next run is exactly the previous report,
          because :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_message_history` skips hidden
          messages,
        * children reading the parent context see the report
          (``is_answer_parent_message``).

        :param manager: Manager that persists the chat.
        :param chat: The agent chat (mutated in place).
        :param report: The message that becomes the document.
        """
        report.is_answer = True
        report.hide = False

        hidden = 0
        for message in chat.messages:
            if message.improvement or message.doc_id == report.doc_id:
                continue
            if not message.hide:
                message.hide = True
                hidden += 1

        manager.save_chat(chat=chat)
        logger.info(
            "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' report is now the document "
            "(%d message(s) hidden)",
            chat.name,
            hidden,
        )

    async def _run_agent(self, chat: Chat, manager: ChatManager):
        """
        Run the agent through a fresh :class:`ChatEngine`.

        A new engine is created per run (same approach as
        :class:`ChatEngineActions`) so the orchestrator never re-enters an
        engine that is already producing a response. ``system`` carries the
        orchestrator framing; the engine appends it to the profile system
        prompt.

        :param chat: Agent chat to process.
        :param manager: Manager owning the chat (settings + event manager).
        :return: The engine result (``(chat, documents)``).
        """
        from codx.junior.chat.chat_engine import ChatEngine

        engine = ChatEngine(
            settings=manager.settings,
            event_manager=manager.event_manager,
            user=None,
        )
        return await engine.chat_with_project(
            chat=chat,
            disable_knowledge=self.disable_knowledge,
            system=ORCHESTRATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        )

    async def run_trigger(self, trigger: AgentTrigger) -> bool:
        """
        Re-invoke one agent task and collapse its answer into the report.

        Steps: re-check the gates on a freshly loaded chat, append the
        ``agent_trigger`` message, run the engine and, when a new report was
        produced, hide everything else. When no report is produced the trigger
        is hidden so the previous watermark is kept and the next cycle retries
        (instead of silently swallowing the completion).

        :param trigger: Trigger to execute.
        :return: True when the agent ran and its report was updated.
        """
        if not _acquire(trigger.agent_id):
            logger.info(
                "agent orchestrator: '%s' is already running; skipping",
                trigger.agent_name,
            )
            return False

        try:
            manager = self._manager(trigger.project_id)
            if manager is None:
                return False

            agent = manager.find_by_id(chat_id=trigger.agent_id)
            if agent is None:
                logger.warning(
                    "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' (%s) not found",
                    trigger.agent_name,
                    trigger.agent_id,
                )
                return False

            if not is_agent_live(agent) or is_loop_paused(agent) or budget_reached(agent):
                logger.info(
                    "agent orchestrator: '%s' became closed, paused or over "
                    "budget before the run; skipping",
                    agent.name,
                )
                return False

            # Snapshot the message ids so the answer produced by THIS run is
            # recognised (hidden reasoning messages are appended too).
            known_ids = {message.doc_id for message in agent.messages}

            trigger_message = Message(
                role="user",
                content=self._build_trigger_content(trigger),
                task_item=TASK_ITEM_AGENT_TRIGGER,
                meta_data={"agent_trigger": True},
            )
            manager.add_message(chat=agent, message=trigger_message)
            self._emit(
                manager,
                agent,
                f"Agent '{agent.name}': {len(trigger.completed)} task(s) "
                "completed, updating report",
            )
            logger.info(
                "agent orchestrator: re-invoking agent '%s' (%s) for %d "
                "completed task(s) in project '%s'",
                agent.name,
                agent.id,
                len(trigger.completed),
                trigger.project_id,
            )

            await self._run_agent(chat=agent, manager=manager)
            manager.save_chat(chat=agent)

            report = next(
                (
                    message for message in reversed(agent.messages)
                    if message.doc_id not in known_ids
                    and message.role == "assistant"
                    and (message.content or "").strip()
                ),
                None,
            )

            if report is None:
                # Nothing usable was produced: hide the trigger so the
                # watermark stays on the previous report and the next cycle
                # retries instead of dropping the completion.
                trigger_message.hide = True
                manager.update_message(chat=agent, message=trigger_message)
                logger.warning(
                    "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' produced no report",
                    agent.name,
                )
                _record_failure(trigger.agent_id)
                return False

            self._collapse_to_single_report(
                manager=manager,
                chat=agent,
                report=report,
            )
            _clear_failure(trigger.agent_id)
            self._emit(manager, agent, "Agent report updated", event_type="done")
            return True

        except Exception as ex:
            _record_failure(trigger.agent_id)
            logger.exception(
                "agent orchestrator: agent '%s' failed: %s",
                trigger.agent_name,
                ex,
            )
            return False
        finally:
            _release(trigger.agent_id)

    async def run_once(self) -> List[AgentTrigger]:
        """
        Detect and execute the pending agent re-invocations of one project.

        Triggers are executed sequentially: agent runs of the same project share
        the project settings object, which the AI runtime stamps with
        ``_active_session`` / ``_current_chat``, so parallel runs would resolve
        each other's chat. Projects are processed in parallel by
        :func:`codx.junior.background.check_agent_tasks`.

        :return: The triggers that were successfully executed.
        """
        triggers = self.collect_triggers()
        if not triggers:
            return []

        logger.info(
            "agent orchestrator: %d agent task(s) to re-invoke in project '%s'",
            len(triggers),
            getattr(self.settings, "project_name", self.project_id),
        )

        executed: List[AgentTrigger] = []
        for trigger in triggers:
            if await self.run_trigger(trigger):
                executed.append(trigger)
        return executed

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from threading import Lock, Thread
from typing import Dict, List

from codx.junior.ai import AIManager
from codx.junior.changes.change_manager import ChangeManager
from codx.junior.globals import (
    CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND,
)
from codx.junior.project.project_discover import (
    find_all_projects
)
from codx.junior.global_settings import read_global_settings
from codx.junior.wiki.wiki_manager import WikiManager

# Setup logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Quarantine settings
QUARANTINE_TRACKER: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
QUARANTINE_LOCK = Lock()
QUARANTINE_DELAYS: List[int] = [0, 1, 10, 30, 120]  # Minutes

# Background process control flag
RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES: bool = True

# Interval between project check cycles (seconds)
PROJECT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS: int = 3

# Maximum number of concurrent project-check threads in the pool
MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS: int = 10

# Wiki full-pipeline rebuild interval (seconds) — runs every 10 minutes
WIKI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS: int = 600

# Tracks last successful wiki build time per project
WIKI_LAST_BUILD: Dict[str, datetime] = {}

# Interval between agent-task cycles (seconds).
#
# This is only the REACTIVITY of the loop: an agent task is re-invoked
# exclusively when one of its descendant tasks reached the "done" status and
# that completion is newer than the agent's last report, so an idle board costs
# nothing but one chat listing per project and cycle.
AGENT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS: int = 15


def start_background_services(stop_event) -> None:
    """
    Start background services for project watching and processing.

    Args:
        stop_event: A threading event used to signal when services should stop.
    """
    if not CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND:
        logger.info("Background services are disabled via CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND.")
        return

    global RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES

    RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES = True
    logger.info("*** Starting background processes ***")
    reload_models()

    # Start the project checking loop in a dedicated background thread
    Thread(target=check_projects, name="ProjectCheckLoop", daemon=True).start()
    # Agent (orchestrator) tasks: re-invoke an `agent` task when one of its
    # children finishes. Same restart-resilient pattern as the project check
    # loop: the trigger state lives in the chats themselves (status_history and
    # the agent's last visible message), so a restart resumes where it stopped.
    Thread(target=check_agent_tasks, name="AgentTaskCheckLoop", daemon=True).start()
    # TODO: Disabled until analyzing high AI consumption. Do not reanable unless you are authorized to
    # Thread(target=check_projects_wiki, name="WikiCheckLoop", daemon=True).start()


async def stop_background_services() -> None:
    """
    Stop all running background services gracefully.
    """
    if not CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND:
        return

    global RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES

    logger.info("Stopping background processes")
    RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES = False


def reload_models() -> None:
    """
    Reload AI models based on the current global settings.
    """
    try:
        AIManager().reload_models(read_global_settings())
        logger.info("AI models reloaded successfully.")
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("Failed to reload AI models: %s", ex)


def is_project_in_quarantine(project_name: str) -> bool:
    """
    Determine if a project is in quarantine based on its last check time and delay schedule.

    Args:
        project_name: The name of the project to check.

    Returns:
        True if the project is currently in quarantine, False otherwise.
    """
    quarantine_info = QUARANTINE_TRACKER.get(project_name)
    if not quarantine_info:
        return False

    delay_index = min(quarantine_info["fail_count"], len(QUARANTINE_DELAYS) - 1)
    delay_minutes = QUARANTINE_DELAYS[delay_index]
    next_allowed_check = quarantine_info["last_checked"] + timedelta(minutes=delay_minutes)
    return datetime.now() < next_allowed_check


def update_quarantine_status(project_name: str, success: bool) -> None:
    """
    Update the quarantine status of a project based on the outcome of the last check.

    Args:
        project_name: The name of the project to update.
        success: True if the last check was successful, False otherwise.
    """
    with QUARANTINE_LOCK:
        quarantine_info = QUARANTINE_TRACKER.setdefault(
            project_name,
            {"fail_count": 0, "last_checked": datetime.min}
        )

        if success:
            quarantine_info["fail_count"] = 0  # Reset failure counter on success
        else:
            quarantine_info["fail_count"] += 1
            logger.info(
                "Adding project to quarantine: %s - error count: %d",
                project_name,
                quarantine_info["fail_count"]
            )

        quarantine_info["last_checked"] = datetime.now()


async def process_project_changes(project) -> None:
    """
    Asynchronously process and handle changes for a single project.

    Args:
        project: The project settings object containing project metadata.
    """
    try:
        session = ChangeManager(settings=project)
        logger.info(">>>>> Checking project: %s", project.project_name)
        await session.process_project_changes()
        update_quarantine_status(project.project_name, success=True)
    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
        update_quarantine_status(project.project_name, success=False)
        project.last_error = str(ex)
        logger.exception("Error processing project changes for %s: %s", project.project_name, ex)


def run_project_check_thread(project) -> None:
    """
    Entry point for a per-project worker in the thread pool.
    Runs the async project change processing in its own isolated event loop,
    since each thread needs its own loop (asyncio loops are not thread-safe).

    Args:
        project: The project settings object to process.
    """
    logger.debug("Thread started for project: %s", project.project_name)
    try:
        # Each thread gets its own event loop to safely run async code
        asyncio.run(process_project_changes(project=project))
    except RuntimeError as ex:
        logger.error(
            "Unhandled runtime error in thread for project %s: %s",
            project.project_name,
            ex
        )
    logger.debug("Thread finished for project: %s", project.project_name)


def check_projects() -> None:
    """
    Continuously checks all projects for updates in parallel using a ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Each non-quarantined project is submitted as a task to the pool, which runs
    `run_project_check_thread` concurrently up to MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS at a time.
    The cycle waits for all submitted tasks to complete before sleeping and repeating.

    """
    while RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES:
        try:
            projects = find_all_projects()
            eligible_projects = [
                project for project in projects.values()
                if not is_project_in_quarantine(project.project_name) \
                    and getattr(project, "watching", True)
            ]

            skipped = len(projects) - len(eligible_projects)
            if skipped:
                logger.debug("Skipping %d quarantined project(s) this cycle.", skipped)

            if not eligible_projects:
                logger.debug("No eligible projects to check this cycle.")
            else:
                logger.info(
                    "Submitting %d project(s) to thread pool (max_workers=%d).",
                    len(eligible_projects),
                    MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS
                )

                # Use a pool so we don't spin up unlimited threads when there are many projects
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(
                    max_workers=MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS,
                    thread_name_prefix="ProjectCheck"
                ) as pool:
                    # Submit one task per eligible project
                    future_to_project = {
                        pool.submit(run_project_check_thread, project): project
                        for project in eligible_projects
                    }

                    # Iterate over futures as they complete to log results promptly
                    for future in as_completed(future_to_project):
                        project = future_to_project[future]
                        try:
                            future.result()  # Re-raise any unhandled exception from the worker
                            logger.debug(
                                "Project check completed successfully: %s",
                                project.project_name
                            )
                        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
                            logger.error(
                                "Project check raised an exception for %s: %s",
                                project.project_name,
                                ex
                            )

        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.exception("Error during project check cycle: %s", ex)

        time.sleep(PROJECT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)


async def process_project_agent_tasks(project) -> None:
    """
    Re-invoke the agent (orchestrator) tasks whose children just finished.

    An `agent` task is re-invoked when a descendant task reached the "done"
    status and that completion is newer than the agent's last report. Pause,
    budget, in-flight and failure-backoff guards live in
    :class:`codx.junior.agent_orchestrator.AgentOrchestrator`.

    Args:
        project: The project settings object to process.
    """
    try:
        # Imported lazily: the orchestrator pulls the chat engine, which must not
        # be loaded while the background module is being imported.
        from codx.junior.agent_orchestrator import AgentOrchestrator

        orchestrator = AgentOrchestrator(settings=project)
        executed = await orchestrator.run_once()
        if executed:
            logger.info(
                "Agent tasks: %d agent(s) re-invoked in project %s",
                len(executed),
                project.project_name,
            )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception(
            "Error processing agent tasks for %s: %s", project.project_name, ex
        )


def run_project_agent_thread(project) -> None:
    """
    Entry point for a per-project agent-task worker in the thread pool.

    Each thread runs its own event loop (asyncio loops are not thread-safe).

    Args:
        project: The project settings object to process.
    """
    try:
        asyncio.run(process_project_agent_tasks(project=project))
    except RuntimeError as ex:
        logger.error(
            "Unhandled runtime error in agent task thread for project %s: %s",
            project.project_name,
            ex
        )


def check_agent_tasks() -> None:
    """
    Continuously re-invokes the agent tasks of every project.

    Projects are processed in parallel (each in its own thread with its own
    event loop) while the agent runs of a single project stay sequential: they
    share the project settings object, which the AI runtime stamps with
    ``_active_session`` / ``_current_chat``.
    """
    while RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES:
        try:
            projects = find_all_projects()
            eligible_projects = list(projects.values())

            if eligible_projects:
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(
                    max_workers=MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS,
                    thread_name_prefix="AgentTaskCheck"
                ) as pool:
                    future_to_project = {
                        pool.submit(run_project_agent_thread, project): project
                        for project in eligible_projects
                    }

                    for future in as_completed(future_to_project):
                        project = future_to_project[future]
                        try:
                            future.result()
                        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
                            logger.error(
                                "Agent task check raised an exception for %s: %s",
                                project.project_name,
                                ex
                            )

        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.exception("Error during agent task check cycle: %s", ex)

        time.sleep(AGENT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)

async def process_project_wiki(project) -> None:
    """
    Run the full wiki pipeline for a project:
      1. Build dependency graph
      2. Detect and build domain pages
      3. Build and index the wiki index
    Only runs when project_wiki is enabled.
    """
    if not getattr(project, "project_wiki", False):
        return
    try:
        logger.info("Wiki pipeline starting for: %s", project.project_name)
        wiki_manager = WikiManager(settings=project)
        graph = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(
            None, wiki_manager.build_dependency_graph
        )
        domains = await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(
            None, wiki_manager.build_domains, graph
        )
        await asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(
            None, wiki_manager.build_wiki_index, graph, domains
        )
        WIKI_LAST_BUILD[project.project_name] = datetime.now()
        logger.info("Wiki pipeline completed for: %s", project.project_name)
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("Wiki pipeline failed for %s: %s", project.project_name, ex)


def run_project_wiki_thread(project) -> None:
    try:
        asyncio.run(process_project_wiki(project=project))
    except RuntimeError as ex:
        logger.error("Wiki thread error for %s: %s", project.project_name, ex)


def check_projects_wiki() -> None:
    """
    Slow background loop that rebuilds the full wiki pipeline for each
    wiki-enabled project once every WIKI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS (10 min).
    """
    while RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES:
        try:
            projects = find_all_projects()
            now = datetime.now()
            eligible = [
                p for p in projects.values()
                if getattr(p, "project_wiki", False)
                and (
                    p.project_name not in WIKI_LAST_BUILD
                    or (now - WIKI_LAST_BUILD[p.project_name]).total_seconds() >= WIKI_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS
                )
            ]
            if eligible:
                logger.info("Wiki pipeline: %d project(s) due for rebuild.", len(eligible))
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS, thread_name_prefix="WikiCheck") as pool:
                    futures = {pool.submit(run_project_wiki_thread, p): p for p in eligible}
                    for future in as_completed(futures):
                        p = futures[future]
                        try:
                            future.result()
                        except Exception as ex:
                            logger.error("Wiki pipeline error for %s: %s", p.project_name, ex)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.exception("Error in wiki check cycle: %s", ex)

        time.sleep(PROJECT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)

## How the flow behaves (test matrix)

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `mode != "agent"` | Untouched — the orchestrator never looks at it |
| Agent chat with no completed child | No run at all (the loop is completion-driven) |
| Child reaches `done` (any nesting level) | Nearest `agent` ancestor re-invoked once with a trigger message |
| Same child completed before the last report | Ignored (watermark) |
| Agent already running | Skipped by the in-flight lock; retried next cycle |
| Newest loop marker is `pause_loop` | Skipped |
| Human replies in the agent chat | Implicit resume |
| `agent.status` = `done` / `rejected` | Skipped (second, independent stop switch) |
| `chat.cost >= chat.estimation_cost` | Skipped and logged; SmolAgent would refuse to spend anyway |
| Run fails / produces no report | Trigger hidden, failure backoff 60s→1h, self-heals |
| After a successful run | New report is `is_answer`, everything else hidden → next run's history is the report |

**Pausing from a client / the API** (no schema change):

```json
POST /api/chats/message
{
  "chat_id": "<agent chat id>",
  "message": { "role": "assistant", "content": "Loop paused: waiting for review", "task_item": "pause_loop" }
}
```

## Known follow-ups (deliberately out of this change set, to keep the diff reviewable)

1. **`project_manager` `pause_loop` / `resume_loop` actions** — so the agent can pause itself in one tool call instead of the model relying on the system prompt.
2. **`parent_id` filter on `list_tasks`** — the agent currently enumerates children through `board`/`column`/`sprint`; a direct parent filter is cheaper and exact.
3. **`append_agent_message` rewrite** — the current agent prompt is still task-shaped ("end this task… return `AGENT_DONE_WORD`"); the orchestrator framing travels via `system=` today. Moving it into the prompt builder is the next polish step.
4. **`switch_project` does not forward `system=`** — a pre-existing gap that only matters when an agent works on a different project than the one that stores it.

def convert_messages_to_prompt(self, messages: List[Union[AIMessage, HumanMessage]]) -> str:
        """
        Convert a list of LangChain messages to a single string prompt for vllm.

        :param messages: List of message objects that needs conversion.
        :return: Formatted string prompt.
        """
        prompt_lines: List[str] = []
        
        for msg in messages:
            # Check message type to assign the correct speaker role
            if msg.type == "ai":
                prompt_lines.append("Assistant: " + str(msg.content))
            else:
                prompt_lines.append("User: " + str(msg.content))
        
        # Append final indicator for the model to start generating
        prompt_lines.append("Assistant:")
        
        return "\n".join(prompt_lines)

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,
message/tool counts, request/chat/run identifiers, HTTP status, provider

timeout, proxy, ...) — always followed by a full traceback. A short Markdown
notice with the same details is also streamed to the client, because previously
a failed connection surfaced as nothing more than the provider's generic
``"Connection error."`` string in both the logs and the chat.

"""
Prompt and message construction for chat interactions.

Extracted from ``ChatEngine`` to keep prompt-building logic (history
rendering, refine/agent prompts, current-request wrapping, and response file
extraction) in one place and reduce the size of the engine module.

The key idea is to demote prior conversation turns to inert *context* so the
model does not re-execute instructions that were already processed:

* Prior turns are wrapped in a ``<conversation_history>`` block and their
  assistant messages are labelled ``<assistant_done>``.
* The live instruction is isolated in a ``<current_request>`` block.

Multimodal content
------------------
Messages with attachments are converted into LangChain messages whose
``content`` is a LIST of parts (``{"type": "text"}`` plus one
``{"type": "image_url"}`` per image). Prompt assembly must therefore only
ever rewrite the TEXT part: stringifying the list would replace the images
with their Python representation and make them invisible to the model.
See :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._get_text_content` /
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._set_text_content`.

Conversation attachments
------------------------
``Message.attachments`` must ALWAYS be visible to the model — not only on the
message that happens to be the current request. Because the history block is
rendered as plain text, images carried by prior turns would otherwise be lost.

:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.collect_attachments` gathers the attachments of EVERY
visible message (parent chats first, then the current chat) and
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_ai_prompt_messages` appends them to the single
``<current_request>`` message:

* ``image/*`` attachments become ``{"type": "image_url"}`` parts,
* every other type (audio notes, documents) is listed in a ``## Attachments``
  text block ONLY, so the model still knows it exists without the request
  carrying an invalid ``image_url`` part.

Attachment payload normalization
--------------------------------
An ``image_url`` part is only useful when the provider can DECODE it. When it
cannot, models do not fail the request: they replace the image with an
``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder, which looks like "the AI cannot see my
screenshots". :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._prepare_attachment` therefore
normalizes every payload before it is sent:

* a ``base64_data`` value that already holds a full ``data:`` URI is not
  prefixed a second time (``data:image/png;base64,data:image/png;base64,...``
  is not decodable),
* whitespace/newlines inside the base64 payload are stripped,
* the media type is resolved from ``file_type`` → data-URI header → file
  extension, so ``application/octet-stream`` / ``image/*`` are never sent,
* only formats vision APIs accept (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF) travel as parts —
  SVG/BMP/TIFF/HEIC are listed in the text block instead,
* oversized screenshots are downscaled/re-encoded (Pillow, best effort,
  cached per payload).

The resulting status of every attachment (mime, size, sent / not sent and
why) is written into the ``## Attachments`` text block.

"""
Parent-agent notification (fire and forget).

An **agent task** is a regular task (chat) whose ``mode`` is
``agent`` (:data:`codx.junior.globals.CHAT_MODE_AGENT`). It acts as the project
manager of the board it lives on: it keeps a single report document and
delegates the real work to the tasks it owns. Instructions and profiles come
from the chat/profiles as usual and the budget is the existing
``Chat.estimation_cost`` / ``Chat.cost`` pair.

This module makes the agent *live*, without any polling service:

* the check happens **once, when a task finishes** — i.e. when
  :meth:`codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager.save_chat` registers a real
  ``status`` transition to ``done`` (writer-agnostic: UI planning PATCH, the
  ``project_manager`` tool and engine runs all go through ``save_chat``);
* the **nearest** ``agent`` ancestor in the board is resolved by walking up
  ``parent_id``;
* the re-invocation is dispatched **fire and forget** (a task on the running
  loop, or a daemon thread when there is none) so the current process finishes
  immediately and never waits for the agent.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[task reaches status done] --> B[save_chat registered the transition]
    B --> C[walk up parent_id - visited set]
    C -->|no agent ancestor| Z[return]
    C -->|agent ancestor| D{agent live?}
    D -->|closed status| Z
    D -->|yes| E{loop paused?}
    E -->|newest loop marker is pause_loop| Z
    E -->|no| F{over budget?}
    F -->|yes| Z
    F -->|no| G{completion newer than the last report?}
    G -->|no| Z
    G -->|yes| H[spawn fire-and-forget notification]
    H --> I[append agent_trigger message]
    I --> J[run the agent through ChatEngine]
    J --> K[collapse the chat to a single report]
```

Design notes
------------
* **No scheduler, no persisted cursor.** The trigger state lives in the chats
  themselves (``status_history`` and the agent's last visible message), so the
  behaviour survives a restart and never needs a background loop.
* **Nearest ancestor only.** Notifying the nearest agent cascades naturally: an
  agent that reaches ``done`` notifies *its* agent ancestor. No fan-out, so a
  task can never be claimed twice.
* **Pause is a message, not a setting.** The loop is paused when the newest
  loop marker of the agent is :data:`~codx.junior.globals.TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP`;
  a human reply or :data:`~codx.junior.globals.TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP` resumes
  it. An assistant answer written after the pause marker does not resume it.
* **One report document.** After a run every message but the new report is
  hidden (and the report is flagged ``is_answer``), so the chat is a document
  that is replaced on every run.
* **The notifier never breaks the caller.** Every entry point swallows its
  errors (they are logged), because it is called from ``save_chat``.

Known limitations (v1):
    * If an agent is already running when a completion arrives, the completion
      is skipped and only logged. The next completion re-evaluates the board.
    * A run that produces no report hides its trigger message, so the agent's
      watermark does not advance and the completion is retried on the next one.
"""

import logging

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

    TASK_ITEM_AGENT_TRIGGER,

from codx.junior.planning_manager import CLOSED_STATUSES, DONE_STATUSES
from codx.junior.project.project_discover import find_project_by_id

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_PARENT_HOPS = 20

AGENT ORCHESTRATOR ROLE
You are the project manager (orchestrator) of a task board. This task IS the

what must happen next. You are re-invoked automatically every time one of your
tasks reaches the "done" status, and your answer replaces the previous report.

def _normalize(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """Lower-case and strip a chat/message field (``None`` becomes ``""``)."""
    return (value or "").strip().lower()


def _parse(value: Optional[str]) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """Parse a timestamp, returning ``None`` instead of ``datetime.min``."""
    parsed = _parse_timestamp(value)
    return None if parsed == datetime.min else parsed


def _is_visible(message: Message) -> bool:
    """Return True when *message* is shown to the user (and to the model)."""
    return not message.hide and not message.improvement


def is_agent(chat: Optional[Chat]) -> bool:
    """Return True when *chat* is an agent (orchestrator) task."""
    return bool(chat) and _normalize(chat.mode) == CHAT_MODE_AGENT

    """
    Return True when the agent may still be re-invoked.

    A closed status (``done`` / ``rejected``) stops the loop, which makes
    "mark the agent as done" a second, independent way to stop it. An empty
    status (new task) is considered live.

    :param chat: The agent task.
    :return: True when the agent is not closed.
    """
    status = _normalize(chat.status)
    return not status or status not in CLOSED_STATUSES


def budget_reached(chat: Chat) -> bool:
    """
    Return True when *chat* already spent its ``estimation_cost``.

    :param chat: Chat whose budget to check.
    :return: True when the accumulated cost reached the estimate.
    """
    limit = getattr(chat, "estimation_cost", None)
    if not limit or limit <= 0:
        return False
    return (getattr(chat, "cost", 0.0) or 0.0) >= limit

    The newest *loop marker* decides. Walking back from the end:

    * :data:`TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP` -> paused,
    * :data:`TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP` -> running,
    * a real user message (not the synthetic orchestrator trigger) -> running
      (implicit resume: someone replied in the chat),
    * anything else (assistant answers, tool scaffolding, hidden messages) is
      skipped.

    This means an assistant answer written *after* the pause marker does not
    resume the loop, while a human reply does.

    :param chat: Full chat (all messages loaded).
    :return: True when the loop is paused.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if message.improvement:
            continue
        task_item = _normalize(message.task_item)
        if task_item == TASK_ITEM_PAUSE_LOOP:

        if task_item == TASK_ITEM_RESUME_LOOP:

    completion performed by the UI, by the ``project_manager`` tool or by an
    engine run is detected exactly the same way.

    :param chat: Chat to inspect.
    :return: Timestamp of the newest ``done`` transition, or ``None``.

    stamps: List[datetime] = []
    for event in chat.status_history or []:
        if _normalize(event.to_status) not in DONE_STATUSES:

        parsed = _parse(event.at)
        if parsed:

    if stamps:

    if _normalize(chat.status) in DONE_STATUSES:

    """
    Return the timestamp of the newest visible message of *chat*.

    This is the watermark of the agent: a completion older than this timestamp

    :param chat: Full chat (all messages loaded).
    :return: Timestamp, or ``None`` when the chat has no visible message.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if not _is_visible(message):
            continue
        return _parse(message.updated_at) or _parse(message.created_at)

def _parent_manager(child: Chat, manager) -> Optional[Any]:

    :param child: The child chat.

    owner_project_id = child.parent_owner_project_id or child.parent_project_id
    settings = getattr(manager, "settings", None)
    current_project_id = getattr(settings, "project_id", None)
    if not owner_project_id or owner_project_id == current_project_id:
        return manager

    project_settings = find_project_by_id(project_id=owner_project_id)
